qs.x: A U-turn is allowed where no sign or marking forbids it and visibility is 100 m in both directions.

qs.q: Is it permitted to drive across the bridge if doing so does not interfere with the driver of the motorcycle?
qs.x: The oncoming-priority sign requires yielding only if entering the narrow section would hinder the oncoming vehicle; if the motorcycle is not hindered, you may cross.

qs.q: After passing the truck, is it permitted to continue in this lane?
qs.x: After passing you must return to the right lane; the left lane is for passing and you may not stay in it.

qs.q: In this situation, is it permitted to continue in the occupied lane?
qs.x: Continuing in the occupied lane is permitted; no marking or sign forbids it, so you may stay in your lane.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a passenger is:
o: A person located in the passenger compartment (cab) of a vehicle or on a vehicle, except the driver and the driving instructor.
A person located in the passenger compartment (cab) of a vehicle or on a vehicle, as well as a person entering or exiting the vehicle, except the driver and the driving instructor.
qs.x: By law a passenger also includes a person boarding or exiting the vehicle, excluding the driver and the driving instructor.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category A vehicles may be issued to:
o: Persons who have reached 16 years of age.
Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
qs.x: A category A license may be issued to persons who have reached 18.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category BE vehicles may be issued to:
o: Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
Persons who have reached 19 years of age.
qs.x: A category BE license may be issued to persons who have reached 19.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a roadway is:
o: An element of a road intended for the movement of vehicles.
An element of a road intended for the movement of non-rail vehicles.
qs.x: A roadway is the road element intended for non-rail vehicles.

qs.q: During driving instruction, must the learner driver wear a seat belt?
o: No, if it makes operating the vehicle difficult.
No, if permitted by the driving instructor.
qs.x: A learner driver must wear a seat belt like any driver; there are no exceptions.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a pedestrian is:
o: A person who is outside a vehicle and on the road, except a person authorized to perform work on the road and performing that work in accordance with the procedure established by law.
A person who is outside a vehicle and on the road, including a person authorized to perform work on the road and performing that work in accordance with the procedure established by law.
qs.x: A pedestrian is a person on the road outside a vehicle, except one authorized to work on the road and doing so.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, initial practical driving instruction is conducted:
o: On roads outside populated areas, taking into account the intensity of vehicle traffic.
On a closed training area or driving range.
On any road, except freeways, taking into account the intensity of vehicle traffic.
qs.x: Initial practical driving instruction takes place on a closed training area or driving range.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, is an exit from an adjacent area onto a road considered an intersection?
qs.x: An exit from an adjacent area onto a road is not considered an intersection.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons holding a driver’s license for categories B, C, and D may also operate those vehicles with trailers if the trailer’s maximum authorized mass does not exceed:
qs.x: With B, C or D licenses you may tow a trailer whose maximum authorized mass does not exceed 750 kg.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, bicyclists are prohibited from riding:
qs.x: Cyclists are prohibited from riding without a helmet; protective eyewear is not required.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category B and C vehicles may be issued to:
o: Persons who have reached 16 years of age.
Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
qs.x: Category B and C licenses may be issued to persons aged 18.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a moped is:
o: A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine displacement not exceeding 50 cm³ and a maximum speed not exceeding 50 km/h.
A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine displacement not exceeding 60 cm³ and a maximum speed not exceeding 60 km/h.
A two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine displacement not exceeding 70 cm³ and a maximum speed not exceeding 70 km/h.
qs.x: A moped is a two- or three-wheeled vehicle with an engine up to 50 cm³ and a top speed up to 50 km/h.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a forced stop is:
o: An interruption of movement caused by the unexpected activation of a prohibitory traffic signal.
An interruption of movement caused by a traffic jam on the road.

Bringing a vehicle to a stationary position because of a vehicle malfunction, the physical and/or mental condition of the driver or passenger, a hazard related to the cargo being transported, or another obstruction that has appeared on the road.
qs.x: A forced stop covers all the listed cases: a sudden prohibitory signal, a traffic jam, a malfunction, or another obstruction.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, insufficient visibility is:
o: The visibility distance of the road during nighttime.
The visibility distance of the road in populated areas when the roadway has no artificial lighting.
Road visibility and/or a visibility distance of up to 300 meters in fog, rain, snowfall, and/or other adverse weather conditions affecting road traffic safety.
qs.x: Insufficient visibility means visibility up to 300 m in fog, rain, snowfall or other adverse weather.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, stopping is:
o: Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for up to 5 minutes, or for the time necessary to pick up or drop off passengers and/or to load or unload the vehicle.
Bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes when this is not related to picking up or dropping off passengers or loading or unloading the vehicle.
qs.x: Stopping is a deliberate halt for up to 5 minutes or for the time needed to board or drop passengers or to load or unload.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a public transit vehicle is:
o: A vehicle that operates along a route, has designated stops, and carries passengers and/or baggage, including a tram, trolleybus, or bus.
A vehicle that operates along a route, has designated stops, and carries passengers and/or baggage, including a tram, trolleybus, or bus, as well as a passenger taxi.
qs.x: Public transit vehicles are trams, trolleybuses and buses running on routes with stops; a taxi is not included.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following are considered equivalent to pedestrians:
o: Persons with disabilities moving in non-motorized wheelchairs.
Persons pulling or pushing a handcart, sled, stroller, or wheelchair.
qs.x: Both people in non-motorized wheelchairs and people pulling or pushing a cart, sled, stroller or wheelchair are treated as pedestrians.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a trailer (semitrailer) is:
o: Any motor vehicle towed by means of a rigid coupling.
A vehicle not equipped with an engine that is designed to be moved by a motor vehicle and to proceed with it as a single unit, including a special-purpose trailer.
qs.x: A trailer is a vehicle without an engine designed to be moved by a motor vehicle and travel with it as one unit.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, traffic on the roads of the Republic of Armenia is:
qs.x: Armenia has right-hand traffic.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, parking is:
o: Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes when this is not related to picking up or dropping off passengers or loading or unloading the vehicle.

Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes, except when necessary to prevent a collision with another road user or an obstruction, to pick up or drop off passengers and/or load or unload the vehicle, or in other cases provided by law.
qs.x: Parking is a deliberate halt of more than 5 minutes, except to avoid a collision, to board or drop passengers, or to load or unload.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons conscripted into the Armed Forces of the Republic of Armenia or other troops may be issued a driver’s license authorizing the operation of category D and subcategory D1 vehicles upon reaching:
qs.x: Conscripts may be issued a category D or subcategory D1 license from age 19.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, within what period from the date a vehicle is acquired must it be presented for state registration to the registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs?
qs.x: A vehicle must be presented for state registration within 15 days of acquisition.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, responsibility for maintaining a vehicle participating in road traffic in technically sound condition is borne by:
o: The owner or user of the vehicle.
The organization that sold the vehicle.
The organization that performed the vehicle’s most recent annual technical inspection.
All of the listed persons and organizations.
qs.x: The owner or user is responsible for keeping the vehicle technically sound, not the seller or the inspection organization.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, before starting to drive, the driver must check:
o: The serviceability of the braking system and steering system.
Whether the remaining tire tread depth meets the established standards.
qs.x: Before driving, the driver must check the brakes and steering and also the remaining tire tread depth.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a driver must provide the vehicle for assistance:
o: To police officers for transporting persons in need of urgent medical care to a medical facility.
To medical personnel proceeding in the same direction to provide medical assistance, with the driver’s consent.
qs.x: A driver must provide the vehicle both to police to transport someone needing urgent care and to medical staff going the same way, with consent.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, if a driver is involved in a road traffic crash, the driver must:
o: Not move objects related to the crash.
Perform all of the listed actions.
qs.x: After a crash the driver must stop immediately, switch on the hazard lights and not move objects related to the crash, so all the listed actions.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the driver of a motor vehicle must carry:
o: A driver’s license authorizing the operation of that category of vehicle and the vehicle registration documents, or, within the Republic of Armenia, their digital versions.
A power of attorney when operating a vehicle belonging to another person.
qs.x: The law requires carrying the license for the vehicle category and the registration documents, or their digital versions; a power of attorney is not part of this requirement.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a traffic lane is:
o: A marked longitudinal strip of the roadway wide enough for vehicles to proceed in a single line.
A marked or unmarked longitudinal strip of the roadway wide enough for vehicles to proceed in a single line.
qs.x: A traffic lane is a marked or unmarked longitudinal strip of the roadway wide enough for a single line of vehicles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, maximum authorized mass is:
o: The mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle.
The mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle, including the driver, passengers and load, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permissible mass.
qs.x: Maximum authorized mass is the manufacturer's limit for a fully equipped and fueled vehicle including driver, passengers and load.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a traffic controller is:
o: A person authorized to regulate road traffic and carrying out that regulation in accordance with the procedure established by law.
Any road user, including a driver, passenger, or pedestrian, who performs traffic-control actions when necessary.
qs.x: A traffic controller is a person authorized by law to regulate traffic, not just any road user.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a bicycle is:
o: A vehicle with at least two wheels, normally propelled by the muscular power of a person on it, particularly by means of pedals or hand cranks, as well as a wheelchair.

A vehicle with at least two wheels, normally propelled by the muscular power of a person on it, particularly by means of pedals or hand cranks, excluding a wheelchair; it may also have an electric motor with a maximum continuous rated power not exceeding 0.25 kW that switches off automatically at speeds above 25 km/h.
qs.x: A bicycle is muscle-powered and may have an electric motor up to 0.25 kW that cuts out above 25 km/h; a wheelchair is excluded.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a person providing driving instruction:
o: Is considered equivalent to a driver.
Is not considered equivalent to a driver.
qs.x: A driving instructor is treated as a driver because the instructor is responsible for the vehicle's operation.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an emergency situation is:
o: A situation caused by the action and/or inaction of a road user in which a real danger of a road traffic crash is created.
A situation caused by the action and/or inaction of a road user and/or traffic controller in which a real danger of a road traffic crash is created.
qs.x: An emergency situation can be caused by the action or inaction of a road user and/or a traffic controller.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, nighttime is:
o: In fall and winter, the period from 8:00 p.m. to 8:00 a.m.; in spring and summer, the period from 10:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m.
The period between the end of evening twilight and the beginning of morning twilight.
The period during which sunlight is absent.
qs.x: Nighttime is the period between the end of evening twilight and the start of morning twilight, not fixed clock hours.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a passenger car is:
o: An automobile with no more than 8 seats intended for passengers and designed and equipped for the safe and comfortable transportation of passengers and baggage.

An automobile with no more than 4 seats intended for passengers, excluding children under 12 years of age, and designed and equipped for the safe and comfortable transportation of passengers and baggage.
qs.x: A passenger car is an automobile with no more than 8 passenger seats.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following are considered equivalent to pedestrians:
o: Persons with disabilities moving at pedestrian speed in motorized wheelchairs.
Persons leading a bicycle, moped, or motorcycle.
qs.x: Both disabled people on motorized wheelchairs at walking speed and people leading a bicycle, moped or motorcycle count as pedestrians.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the right to operate a vehicle arises:
o: Upon successfully passing the practical driving examination at the registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
qs.x: The right to drive arises upon receiving the driver's license, not upon passing the exam.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, international driving permits authorizing the operation of category A and B vehicles may be issued to:
o: Persons who have reached 16 years of age.
Persons who have reached 17 years of age.
Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
qs.x: International permits for categories A and B are issued from age 18.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an international driving permit authorizing the operation of category C vehicles may be issued to:
o: Persons who have reached 18 years of age.
Persons who have reached 20 years of age.
Persons who have reached 21 years of age.
qs.x: An international permit for category C is issued from age 21.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a national driver’s license is issued for:
qs.x: A national driver's license is issued for 10 years.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an international driving permit is issued for:
qs.x: An international driving permit is issued for 3 years.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a person may become a driver candidate, except a candidate for a subcategory AM vehicle, upon reaching:
qs.x: A person may become a driver candidate (except for AM) from age 17.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, stopping is:
o: Bringing a vehicle to a stationary position in response to a passenger’s request.
Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for more than 5 minutes when this is not related to picking up or dropping off passengers or loading or unloading the vehicle.
Intentionally bringing a vehicle to a stationary position for up to 5 minutes, or for the time necessary to pick up or drop off passengers and/or to load or unload the vehicle.
qs.x: Stopping is a deliberate halt of up to 5 minutes or as long as boarding or loading takes; beyond 5 minutes it is parking.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the maximum authorized mass of a vehicle is:
o: The maximum mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle.
The mass of a fully equipped and fueled vehicle loaded with the driver, passengers, and cargo, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permitted mass.
The mass of a vehicle loaded with the driver, passengers, and cargo, established by the manufacturer as the maximum permitted mass.
qs.x: Maximum authorized mass is the manufacturer-set mass of a fully equipped, fueled vehicle loaded with driver, passengers and cargo.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons authorized to operate category B, C, and D vehicles and subcategory C1 and D1 vehicles may also operate them with trailers if the trailer’s maximum authorized mass is:
qs.x: With those categories you may tow a trailer with a maximum authorized mass of 750 kg.

qs.q: When entering a road with an asphalt-concrete surface from an unpaved road, the asphalt-concrete road:
o: Must be considered the priority road.
Must be considered a road of equal priority.
qs.x: When entering a paved road from an unpaved road, the paved road is the priority road and you must yield.

qs.q: How many traffic lanes are there on this roadway?
qs.x: The single solid line in the middle divides the roadway into two lanes, one for each direction.

qs.q: Under the indicated roadway width, is it permitted to proceed along the center of the roadway?
o: Yes, when there is no oncoming traffic.
qs.x: A 7 m roadway has two lanes, so you must drive in the right lane, not the center, even with no oncoming traffic.

qs.q: Which of the following stationary objects is not considered an obstruction?
o: An automobile stopped because of traffic congestion.
qs.x: A car stopped in a traffic jam is part of the traffic flow, not an obstruction; road damage, a foreign object and a disabled car are.

qs.q: Are the sidewalk and shoulders considered part of the road?
qs.x: A road includes the roadway, sidewalks, shoulders and medians, so both sidewalks and shoulders are part of the road.

qs.q: How many roadways does this road have?
qs.x: The grassy median in the picture splits the road into two separate roadways.

qs.q: How many intersections are shown in this image?
qs.x: The roads meet at a single place, so this is one intersection even though the crossing road has a median.

qs.q: How many intersections of roadways are there at this intersection?
qs.x: The crossing road has a median, meaning two roadways, so two roadway crossings occur here.

qs.q: How many traffic lanes does this road have?
qs.x: The road has two roadways, each with two lanes, for four traffic lanes in total.

qs.q: In which image does the road have a median?
qs.x: In both pictures opposing directions are separated by a median, which may be structural or defined by markings.

qs.q: To yield to other vehicles means that:
o: The driver must not continue or resume driving or perform any maneuver if doing so could force the drivers of other vehicles to change direction or speed.
The driver must not continue or resume driving or perform any maneuver if doing so could force the drivers of other vehicles to unexpectedly change direction or speed.
The driver must stop the vehicle unconditionally.
qs.x: Yielding means not continuing or starting a maneuver if it would force others to change direction or speed unexpectedly; stopping is not always required.

qs.q: In which image is an intersection shown?
qs.x: An intersection is where roads cross or join; the left picture shows roads joining, while the right is a plain straight section.

qs.q: How many intersections of roadways are there at the intersection?
qs.x: The crossing road has a median, so our roadway crosses two roadways.

qs.q: A lane change means:
o: Leaving the traffic lane occupied by the vehicle while maintaining the original direction of movement.
Leaving the row occupied by the vehicle within a marked traffic lane while maintaining the original direction of movement.
qs.x: A lane change covers leaving the occupied lane and also leaving a row within a marked lane, keeping the original direction.

qs.q: A turn means:
o: A maneuver performed for the purpose of entering another road.
A maneuver performed for the purpose of entering another road or an adjacent area from the road.
qs.x: A turn is a maneuver made to enter another road or an adjacent area from the road.

qs.q: A U-turn means:
o: Driving a vehicle in the opposite direction.
A maneuver performed for the purpose of changing the vehicle’s direction of movement to the opposite direction.
qs.x: A U-turn is a maneuver done to reverse the direction of travel, not just driving in the opposite direction.

qs.q: Passing without leaving the lane means:
o: Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles without leaving the occupied lane.
Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving the occupied lane.
qs.x: Passing without leaving the lane is advancing ahead of vehicles without leaving your lane; leaving the lane makes it overtaking.

qs.q: Starting to move means:
o: The moment a vehicle begins moving from a stopping or parking location, with or without changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
The moment a vehicle begins moving from a stopping or parking location while changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
qs.x: Starting to move is pulling away from a stop or parking spot, with or without moving into an adjacent lane.

qs.q: Maneuvering means:
o: Starting to move a vehicle (involving entry into an adjacent traffic lane), changing lanes, changing direction, stopping (with a lane change), and backing.
Starting to move a vehicle, changing lanes, changing direction, stopping, and backing.
qs.x: Maneuvering includes starting to move (with entering an adjacent lane), changing lanes, changing direction, stopping with a lane change, and reversing.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a truck is:
o: An automobile designed by its construction and equipment for the transportation of cargo.
An automobile weighing more than 3.5 metric tons and designed by its construction and equipment for the transportation of cargo.
qs.x: A truck is any automobile designed and equipped to carry cargo; there is no 3.5 t weight condition in the definition.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a median is:
o: A structurally separated road element that divides adjacent roadways and is not intended for vehicle or pedestrian traffic or stopping.
A road element that divides adjacent roadways, is separated structurally and/or by appropriate pavement markings, and is not intended for vehicle or pedestrian traffic or stopping.
qs.x: A median may be separated structurally and/or by markings and is not meant for travel or stopping.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a vehicle is:
o: A device designed to transport a person, cargo, or equipment installed on it along a road.
qs.x: A vehicle is any device designed to carry people, cargo or mounted equipment on a road, not just cars and motorcycles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following persons are considered equivalent to drivers:
o: A person driving pack and/or riding animals or livestock along a road.
A person driving pack and/or riding animals or livestock.
qs.x: A person driving pack or riding animals or livestock along a road is treated as a driver.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the following are considered equivalent to motorcycles:
o: Three-wheeled motor vehicles with a mass of up to 400 kg in fully equipped and fueled condition, excluding the driver, cargo, and passengers.
Quadricycles with a motorcycle-type seating position or motorcycle-type handlebars.
qs.x: Quadricycles with a motorcycle-type seat or handlebars are treated as motorcycles.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a sidewalk is:
o: A road element adjacent to the roadway and intended for pedestrian movement in accordance with the procedure established by law.
A road element separated from the roadway in any manner and intended for pedestrian movement in accordance with the procedure established by law.
qs.x: A sidewalk is a road element for pedestrians that may adjoin the roadway or be separated from it.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, an automobile is:
o: A motor vehicle designed for transporting people or cargo on a road, or for towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, excluding vehicles such as agricultural tractors for which transporting people or cargo on a road, or towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, is only an additional function.

A motor vehicle designed for transporting people or cargo on a road, or for towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, including vehicles such as agricultural tractors for which transporting people or cargo on a road, or towing a vehicle used to transport cargo, is only an additional function.
qs.x: Agricultural tractors, for which carrying or towing is only a secondary function, are excluded from the definition of an automobile.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a national driver’s license of the Republic of Armenia authorizing the operation of Category “A” vehicles also authorizes the operation of:
o: Vehicles of subcategory “B1” having a motorcycle-type seat or handlebar.
qs.x: A category A license also covers subcategories A1, AM and B1 with a motorcycle-type seat or handlebars.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, a national driver’s license of the Republic of Armenia authorizing the operation of Category “B” vehicles also authorizes the operation of:
o: Vehicles of subcategory “B1,” except vehicles having a motorcycle-type seat or handlebar.
qs.x: A category B license covers subcategory B1 (except motorcycle-type vehicles); AM is separate.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, international driving permits issued by the competent authorities of the Republic of Armenia are considered, for purposes of driving vehicles within the territory of the Republic of Armenia:
qs.x: International permits issued by Armenia are not valid inside Armenia; they are for driving abroad.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, the right to drive vehicles arises:
o: Upon receipt of the driver’s license.
Upon assignment of the digital version of the driver’s license.
qs.x: The right to drive arises both on receiving the license and on assignment of its digital version.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, driver’s licenses obtained in other countries by citizens of the Republic of Armenia, including dual citizens, that comply with the requirements for driver’s licenses under the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic and its subsequent amendments and supplements are considered valid within the territory of the Republic of Armenia, from the date those persons enter the Republic of Armenia, for:
qs.x: Licenses from abroad meeting the Vienna Convention are valid in Armenia for three months from entry.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, persons applying for a driver’s license for the first time to operate vehicles of which of the following categories must submit to the registration and examination division of the Ministry of Internal Affairs a certificate confirming that they have undergone medical certification?
qs.x: A medical certification certificate is required when first applying for categories C, D and T.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, if a driver candidate undergoing practical driving instruction violates the traffic rules, liability in accordance with the law is borne by:
o: The driving instructor of the training center or the person providing individual practical driving instruction.
qs.x: During practical instruction the instructor, not the driver candidate, bears liability for traffic violations.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, when may an 18- year-old who holds a national driver’s license for Categories “B” and “C” obtain an international driving permit for the same categories?
o: At the same time as the national driver’s license is obtained.
qs.x: An international permit for categories B and C can be obtained only after turning 21.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, when may a 19- year-old who holds a national driver’s license for Categories “BE” and “CE” obtain an international driving permit for the same categories?
o: At the same time as the national driver’s license is obtained.
qs.x: An international permit for BE and CE can be obtained after turning 21.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, is a person holding a driver’s license for subcategory “C1” permitted to drive a truck whose maximum authorized mass exceeds 8500 kg?
qs.x: Subcategory C1 allows trucks up to 8500 kg maximum authorized mass; heavier trucks are not permitted.

qs.q: According to the Law of the Republic of Armenia on Ensuring Road Traffic Safety, which of the following may be operated on public roads?
qs.x: A quadricycle may be used on public roads, while an all-terrain quad bike may not.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The remaining tread depth of the tires of a passenger car is 1.8 mm.
The hydraulic brake system is not leak-tight.
qs.x: A leaking hydraulic brake system prohibits operation, while 1.8 mm of tread is still legal for a passenger car (minimum 1.6 mm).

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The remaining tread depth of the tires of a truck is 1.6 mm.
The pressure gauge of the pneumatic brake system does not operate.
qs.x: A non-working pneumatic brake pressure gauge prohibits operation, while 1.6 mm tread on a truck is still legal (minimum 1.0 mm).

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: There is movement in steering parts or assemblies that is not provided for by the design, or threaded connections are not tightened.
A fire extinguisher is missing from a truck.
qs.x: Unintended play in steering parts or loose threaded joints, and a missing fire extinguisher on a truck, each prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The exterior lighting devices do not operate in the prescribed mode.
The remaining tread depth of the tires of a motorcycle is 0.6 mm.
qs.x: Faulty exterior lights and a motorcycle tread of 0.6 mm (minimum 0.8 mm) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The rear fog lights are connected to the vehicle’s brake lights.
The engine coolant temperature gauge does not operate.
qs.x: Rear fog lights wired to the brake lights prohibit operation; a faulty coolant temperature gauge is not on the prohibition list.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The tires have localized damage exposing the tire cord.
The interior lighting devices of a passenger car do not operate.
In all of the listed cases.
qs.x: Localized tire damage exposing the cord prohibits operation; dead interior lights do not.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: A motorcycle without a sidecar does not have an emergency warning triangle.
The tires do not correspond to the vehicle model in size or permitted load capacity.
qs.x: Tires that do not match the model's size or load rating prohibit operation; a motorcycle without a sidecar does not require a warning triangle.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Even one wheel-fastening bolt is missing.
Tires with different tread patterns are installed on the same axle.
qs.x: A single missing wheel-fastening bolt and tires with different tread patterns on one axle both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The head restraints provided by the vehicle’s design are missing.
New and retreaded tires are installed on the same axle.
qs.x: Missing head restraints and new plus retreaded tires on one axle both prohibit operation under the list.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The content of harmful substances in the exhaust gases exceeds the limits established by the legislation of the Republic of Armenia.
The footrests provided by the motorcycle’s design are missing.
qs.x: Exceeding exhaust emission limits and missing motorcycle footrests both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The engine crankcase ventilation system is not leak-tight.
The engine fuel system is not leak-tight.
qs.x: A leak in the crankcase ventilation or in the fuel system each prohibits operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The engine crankcase ventilation system is not leak-tight.
Winter and non-winter tires are installed on the same axle.
qs.x: A leaking crankcase ventilation system and mixing winter and non-winter tires on one axle both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The windshield washers provided by the vehicle’s design do not operate.
The engine’s external noise level exceeds the limits established by the standard.
qs.x: Non-working windshield washers and excessive engine noise both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The rear fog lights are not connected to the brake lights.
The windshield washers provided by the vehicle’s design do not operate.
In all of the listed cases.
qs.x: Of these, only non-working windshield washers prohibit operation; rear fog lights not tied to the brake lights is correct.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Items or objects that may cause injury to road users are installed on the vehicle.
qs.x: Installed objects that could injure road users and a non-working horn both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: There is excessive play in the connections between the motorcycle frame and the sidecar frame.
Yellow-light fog lamps are installed at the front.
qs.x: Play in the motorcycle and sidecar frame joints prohibits operation, while yellow front fog lamps are allowed.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: A first-aid kit is missing from a truck.
White reflectors are installed at the front.
qs.x: A missing first-aid kit on a truck prohibits operation, while white front reflectors are normal.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: A first-aid kit is missing from a motorcycle with a sidecar.
The trailer support-coupling device is defective.
qs.x: A missing first-aid kit on a sidecar motorcycle and a defective coupling device both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The seat belts provided by the vehicle’s design do not operate.
Items or objects that restrict the driver’s field of vision are installed within the driver’s field of view.
qs.x: Non-working seat belts and objects blocking the driver's view both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Changes or modifications have been made to the vehicle’s design without permission from the vehicle registration authority.
Yellow-light turn signals are installed at the front.
qs.x: Unauthorized structural modifications prohibit operation, while yellow front turn signals are permitted.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: A motor vehicle used for practical driving instruction does not have the required identification sign.
The fuel gauge does not operate.
qs.x: A training vehicle without its identification sign may not be operated; a broken fuel gauge is not on the prohibition list.

qs.q: A motorcycle may not be operated if:
o: The safety bars provided by its design are missing.
The minimum remaining tire tread depth is 1.6 mm.
qs.x: Missing safety bars prohibit operation, while 1.6 mm tread is acceptable for a motorcycle.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Yellow-light turn signals are installed at the front.
Even one wheel-fastening bolt is missing.
qs.x: Even one missing wheel-fastening bolt prohibits operation, while yellow front turn signals are normal.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Amber-light turn signals are installed at the front.
The trailer towing device is defective.
qs.x: A defective towing device prohibits operation, while amber front turn signals are allowed.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: White reflectors are installed at the front.
The trailer towing device is defective.
qs.x: A defective towing device prohibits operation, while white front reflectors are normal.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The seat belts provided by the vehicle’s design are missing.
White-light backup lamps are installed at the rear.
qs.x: Missing seat belts prohibit operation, while white reversing lamps at the rear are correct.

qs.q: A motorcycle with a sidecar may not be operated if:
o: The transverse passenger handhold on the seat, as provided by the design, is missing.
The remaining tire tread depth is 0.6 mm.
In all of the listed cases.
qs.x: For a sidecar motorcycle, a missing passenger handhold, a missing first-aid kit and 0.6 mm tread each prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The interior lighting devices of a passenger car do not operate.
The head restraints provided by the vehicle’s design are missing.
qs.x: Missing head restraints prohibit operation, while dead interior lights in a passenger car do not.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Red reflectors are installed at the rear.
The speedometer provided by the vehicle’s design does not operate.
qs.x: A non-working speedometer prohibits operation, while red rear reflectors are normal.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The total play in the steering system of a passenger car exceeds 10 degrees.
The mud flaps and splash guards provided by the vehicle design are missing.
qs.x: Steering play above 10 degrees and missing mud flaps and splash guards both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: A first-aid kit is missing from a passenger car.
Red-light backup lamps are installed at the rear.
qs.x: A missing first-aid kit and red reversing lamps (they must be white) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The remaining tread depth of the tires on a passenger-car trailer is less than 1.6 mm.
Amber-light turn signals are installed at the rear.
qs.x: Trailer tread below 1.6 mm prohibits operation, while amber rear turn signals are allowed.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The hydraulic brake system is not leak-tight.
White-light turn signals are installed at the rear.
qs.x: A leaking hydraulic brake system and white rear turn signals (they must be amber or red) both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Tires of different constructions are installed on the same axle.
The engine fuel system is not leak-tight.
qs.x: Tires of different construction on one axle and a leaking fuel system both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The cooling system does not maintain a stable operating temperature for the engine.
qs.x: A non-working horn prohibits operation; the cooling system condition is not the listed prohibition here.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: There is movement in steering parts or assemblies that is not provided for by the design.
White-light turn signals are installed at the front.
qs.x: Unintended play in steering parts prohibits operation; this is the correct option.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The tires have localized damage exposing the tire cord.
qs.x: Localized tire damage exposing the cord prohibits operation.

qs.q: A passenger-car may not be operated if:
o: The remaining tire tread depth is 2.2 mm.
qs.x: A missing first-aid kit prohibits operation, while 2.2 mm tread is legal (minimum 1.6 mm).

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: For a bus built on a passenger-car chassis, the total play in the steering system exceeds 10 degrees.
The mudguards and splash guards provided by the vehicle’s design are missing.
qs.x: Steering play over 10 degrees and missing mudguards and splash guards both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The cargo-bed door latch provided by the vehicle’s design does not operate.
The cab door latch provided by the vehicle’s design does not operate.
qs.x: A non-working cargo-bed door latch or cab door latch each prohibits operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Red-light turn signals are installed at the rear.
The rear protective device provided by the vehicle’s design is missing.
qs.x: A missing rear protective device prohibits operation, while red rear turn signals are allowed.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The power steering system provided by the vehicle’s design is defective or missing.
The car audio system is not functioning.
qs.x: A defective or missing power steering unit prohibits operation, while a broken car audio system does not.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The parking brake system does not hold the vehicle stationary on the gradient specified by the standard.
The leak-tightness of the transmission seals is compromised.
qs.x: A parking brake that cannot hold the vehicle on the specified slope and leaking transmission seals both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The spare-wheel holder does not operate.
The leak-tightness of the rear-axle seals is compromised.
qs.x: A faulty spare-wheel holder and leaking rear-axle seals both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: There are visible tears in the webbing of the seat belts provided by the vehicle’s design.
The vehicle is not equipped with fog lamps.
qs.x: Visible tears in seat belt webbing prohibit operation, while lacking fog lamps does not.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The engine-hood latch provided by the vehicle’s design does not operate.
The rear side windows are curtained and two side rear-view mirrors are installed.
qs.x: A non-working hood latch prohibits operation, while curtained rear side windows are fine if both side mirrors are present.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The rear side windows are curtained and two side rear-view mirrors are missing.
The window heating and defogging devices provided by the vehicle’s design do not operate.
qs.x: Curtained rear windows without side mirrors and non-working window heating and defogging both prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The fuel-tank cap provided by the vehicle’s design does not operate.
The front side windows are curtained.
qs.x: A faulty fuel-tank cap and curtained front side windows each prohibit operation, so both apply.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The windows provided by the vehicle’s design are missing.
qs.x: A non-working horn and missing design-provided windows each prohibit operation, so both apply.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: There are cracks in a wheel rim or wheel disc.
There are visible distortions in the shape or dimensions of the wheel-rim mounting holes.
qs.x: Cracks in the rim or wheel disc and visibly deformed mounting holes each prohibit operation, so both apply.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The exterior lighting devices and reflectors are dirty.
The front and rear protective devices are dirty.
qs.x: Dirty exterior lights and reflectors reduce visibility and prohibit operation, whereas dirty protective devices do not.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Lamps or lenses are missing from the lighting devices.
Lenses or lamps that do not correspond to the type of the lighting device are used.
qs.x: Missing lamps or lenses, and lamps or lenses not matching the type of light, each prohibit operation.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The exterior lighting devices and reflectors are dirty.
Exterior lighting devices from a different make of vehicle are installed on a discontinued vehicle.
qs.x: Dirty lights and reflectors prohibit operation, but fitting another make's lights on a discontinued vehicle is allowed.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Tires with different tread patterns are installed on the same axle.
The remaining tire tread depth of a passenger car is 1.6 mm.
qs.x: Different tread patterns on one axle prohibit operation, while 1.6 mm on a passenger car is still the legal minimum.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The remaining tire tread depth of a truck is 1.4 mm.
Yellow reflectors are installed at the front.
qs.x: Yellow front reflectors are prohibited (front must be white), while 1.4 mm tread on a truck is legal (minimum 1.0 mm).

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Yellow reflectors are installed at the rear.
Yellow reflectors are installed at the front.
qs.x: Yellow reflectors are not allowed at the front (must be white) or at the rear (must be red).

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: An “Oversized Cargo” identification sign with white and red reflective stripes is installed at the rear.
The remaining tire tread depth of a moped is 0.7 mm.
qs.x: A moped needs at least 0.8 mm of tread, so 0.7 mm prohibits operation; the described sign installation also fails the requirements.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: The “Doctor” identification sign is missing from an automobile driven by a physician-driver.
The fuel-tank cap provided by the vehicle’s design does not operate.
qs.x: A faulty fuel-tank cap prohibits operation; a missing Doctor sign does not.

qs.q: A vehicle may not be operated if:
o: Tires with different tread patterns are installed on the same axle.
A “Transportation of Children” identification sign with a yellow reflective background and red reflective border is installed at the front.
qs.x: Different tread patterns on one axle prohibit operation, but the Transportation of Children sign belongs at front and rear.

qs.q: When making a right turn, is it permitted to enter the lane indicated by this sign?
o: Permitted if the lane is not separated from the rest of the roadway by a solid pavement marking.
qs.x: The blue sign with an arrow and a bus marks a transit-vehicle lane; entering it to make a right turn is allowed unless it is separated by a solid marking line.

qs.q: This traffic sign indicates:
o: A section of road where a sidewalk or pedestrian path is present.
A section of road where a pedestrian crossing is present.
A section of road where there is no sidewalk or pedestrian path.
qs.x: The red triangle shows a pedestrian walking over zebra stripes, so it warns of a pedestrian crossing.

qs.q: Which sign prohibits vehicles from proceeding with a distance between them that is less than the distance shown on the sign?
qs.x: Sign 3, a red circle with two cars and 70 m, prohibits driving closer to the vehicle ahead than the stated distance.

qs.q: Within populated areas, how far before a hazardous section of road are these signs installed?
qs.x: Warning signs like these red triangles are placed 50–100 m before the hazard in built-up areas.

qs.q: This traffic sign:
o: Prohibits all motor vehicles except two-wheeled motorcycles without sidecars.
Prohibits all vehicles except wheeled tractors.
qs.x: The tractor silhouette in a red circle prohibits tractors and self-propelled machinery.

qs.q: Which sign requires a driver to yield to vehicles entering or approaching the narrow section of road from the opposite direction?
qs.x: Sign 3 shows a red oncoming arrow against our black arrow, requiring us to yield to oncoming traffic at the narrow section.

qs.q: Which sign warns of an approaching intersection of roads of equal priority?
qs.x: Sign 5, the X in a triangle, warns of an intersection of equal roads, whereas the others show a side road meeting the main road.

qs.q: Which sign is installed immediately before the intersection of roadways?
qs.x: Priority-regulating signs are placed right before the crossing of roadways, and sign 2 is the one that fits.

qs.q: These signs permit traffic:
o: Straight ahead, to the right, and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The red-ringed sign with the left-arrow plaque restricts only the left direction, so straight, right and a U-turn remain permitted.

qs.q: Which sign gives a driver the right-of-way over oncoming vehicles?
qs.x: Sign 4 is a blue square with a large white up arrow and a small red down arrow: our direction has priority over oncoming traffic.

qs.q: What does the supplemental plaque below the sign indicate?
o: The distance from the sign to the beginning of the first turn.
The distance from the first turn to the beginning of the second turn.
The length of the road section with hazardous turns.
qs.x: The 100 m plaque with arrows at both ends under the winding-road triangle shows the length of the hazardous section.

qs.q: What does the following combination of signs indicate?
o: Motorcycle traffic to the right is prohibited.
Motorcycle traffic to the right is permitted.
qs.x: The red-ringed motorcycle sign with the right-arrow plaque prohibits motorcycles from going to the right.

qs.q: Which sign prohibits parking on even-numbered days of the month?
qs.x: Sign 5, the crossed blue disc with two vertical bars, prohibits parking on even dates, while sign 4 with one bar is for odd dates.

qs.q: This traffic sign:
o: Permits driving only at the indicated speed or higher.
Prohibits driving at a speed higher than the speed shown on the sign.
Indicates the speed recommended for driving on this section of road.
qs.x: A blue disc with a number is a minimum-speed sign: driving is allowed only at that speed or faster.

qs.q: Which of the following signs requires a driver to yield to oncoming vehicles?
qs.x: Sign 2, the red circle with a black and a red arrow, requires yielding to oncoming traffic at a narrow section.

qs.q: This sign is called:
o: Advance indication for going around an obstruction.
Advance indication for changing to another roadway.
Advance indication for entering the oncoming traffic lane.
qs.x: The yellow temporary sign with an arrow leading across to the other carriageway is the advance indication of changing to another roadway.

qs.q: Which sign requires a driver to yield to vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road?
qs.x: Sign 3, the inverted red-bordered triangle (Yield), requires giving way to traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Which of the following signs permits driving only at the indicated speed or higher (km/h)?
qs.x: Sign 3, the blue disc with 50, is a minimum-speed sign, while sign 1 in a red ring is a maximum limit.

qs.q: Which sign indicates a section of one-way road?
qs.x: Sign 3, a blue square with one large white arrow, marks a one-way road.

qs.q: What does the supplemental plaque used with the main sign indicate?
o: The length of the narrow section of road.
The distance from the sign to the location where the restriction begins.
The distance to the location for going around the narrow section of road.
qs.x: The 300 m plaque under the width-limit sign shows the distance from the sign to where the restriction begins.

qs.q: This traffic sign warns that ahead there is:
o: A road section with a water crossing that has no bridge or ferry.
A road section crossing water by means of a drawbridge.
A location where the road reaches a riverbank or shoreline.
qs.x: The triangle shows a car at the edge of a quay above waves, warning that the road runs out onto a riverbank or shore.

qs.q: Which of the following indicates the area of effect of traffic signs prohibiting stopping and parking?
qs.x: The white plaque with an arrow and a distance in metres (plaque 4) shows the length of the zone where the stop and parking bans apply.

qs.q: Which sign indicates the length of a hazardous road section covered by the warning signs?
qs.x: Plaque 4, white with arrows at both ends and 100 m, gives the length of the hazardous stretch covered by the warning signs.

qs.q: This traffic sign indicates:
o: A one-way road on which only trucks are permitted.
A lane designated only for trucks.
The recommended direction of traffic for trucks.
qs.x: The blue sign with an up arrow and a truck shows the recommended direction of travel for trucks.

qs.q: Which sign indicates a “Hotel” or “Motel”?
qs.x: Sign 3, a bed on blue, means Hotel or Motel, whereas sign 1 with a red cross is a hospital.

qs.q: Vehicles displaying this identification sign are:
o: Driven by deaf or deaf-mute drivers.
Driven by drivers with less than 3 years of driving experience.
qs.x: The yellow disc with three black dots is the identification sign for deaf or deaf-mute drivers.

qs.q: Which sign indicates the end of a zone with a maximum speed limit of 50 km/h?
qs.x: Sign 2, the black-ringed disc with a grey 50 struck by diagonal lines, marks the end of the maximum-speed zone.

qs.q: What do this sign and supplemental plaque warn about?
o: Stopping on the shoulder is prohibited because of roadwork.
Entering the shoulder is dangerous because of roadwork.
Parking on the shoulder is prohibited because of roadwork.
qs.x: The triangle shows a worker digging and the plaque shows a car on the shoulder: driving onto the shoulder is dangerous due to roadwork.

qs.q: Vehicles displaying this identification sign are:
o: Driven by deaf or deaf-mute drivers.
qs.x: The rectangular plate with white and red fields is the identification sign of a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo.

qs.q: Which sign cancels all previously imposed restrictions?
qs.x: Sign 4, the plain white disc with black diagonal stripes, cancels all previously imposed restrictions.

qs.q: In which case has the driver correctly complied with the requirements of this sign?
o: The driver yielded to motor vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road.
The driver yielded to vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The inverted-triangle Yield sign requires giving way to all vehicles on the intersecting road, not only motor vehicles.

qs.q: Which of the displayed signs is used as the identification sign for a road train?
qs.x: The three orange lamps on the cab roof of the right-hand truck are the road-train sign; the orange triangle on the left truck is a different sign.

qs.q: Which sign requires a driver to yield to vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road?
qs.x: Sign 4, the inverted red-bordered triangle, is Yield and requires giving way to traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Which of the following signs (supplemental plaques) indicates how a vehicle must be positioned when parked?
qs.x: Plaque 3 shows a car with its wheels on the kerb or sidewalk, i.e. how the vehicle must be positioned when parked.

qs.q: Is it permitted to stop in the lane indicated by this sign to pick up passengers?
o: Permitted if the lane is located along the right edge of the roadway and is not separated from the rest of the roadway by a solid pavement marking.
qs.x: The blue sign with an arrow and a bus marks a transit lane; stopping to pick up passengers is allowed if it is on the right edge and not separated by a solid line.

qs.q: When this traffic sign is present:
o: Passing by all types of vehicles is prohibited, except when passing slow-moving vehicles, animal- drawn carts, two-wheeled motorcycles without sidecars, mopeds, and bicycles.
Trucks with a maximum authorized mass not exceeding 3.5 metric tons are permitted to pass.
Passing is permitted if the speed of the passing vehicle does not exceed 30 km/h.
qs.x: The sign with a red car beside a black car prohibits overtaking, except of slow vehicles, animal carts, solo motorcycles, mopeds and bicycles.

qs.q: Which sign indicates “Intersection with a Bicycle Path”?
qs.x: Sign 2, the triangle with a bicycle, warns of a bicycle-path crossing, whereas the blue disc 1 marks the bicycle path itself.

qs.q: Which sign indicates the end of the no-passing zone?
qs.x: Sign 1, two cars crossed by diagonal stripes, marks the end of the no-passing zone.

qs.q: Which sign indicates the permitted directions of traffic at a T-intersection?
qs.x: Permitted directions at an intersection are shown by a blue arrow sign, while the chevron board, dead-end and side-road signs mean something else.

qs.q: This traffic sign indicates:
o: The direction of traffic toward a destination located within a populated area.
The end of an acceleration lane or an additional lane on an uphill grade.
qs.x: The blue square with a white T-shape and a red bar on top is the dead-end sign.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted within the area where this sign is in effect?
o: Vehicles whose maximum speed exceeds 40 km/h.
qs.x: The blue sign with a white car marks a road for automobiles, where cars and motorcycles are allowed.

qs.q: Which of these traffic signs is not a prohibitory sign?
qs.x: Sign 2, the inverted triangle (Yield), is a priority sign, while the others in red rings or with a red cross are prohibitory.

qs.q: What does this identification sign indicate?
o: Ahead is a section of road with an uneven roadway surface.
Ahead is a section of road with three lanes for traffic in this direction.
The motor vehicle is equipped with studded tires.
qs.x: The letter Ш in the red triangle shows the vehicle is fitted with studded tyres.

qs.q: Which sign is called “End of One-Way Road”?
qs.x: Sign 4, a blue square with a white arrow slashed by a red diagonal, means end of one-way road.

qs.q: Which sign requires a driver to yield to vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road?
qs.x: Sign 2, the inverted triangle, requires giving way to vehicles on the intersecting road.

qs.q: The following signs indicate:
o: A parking place 30 meters away for automobiles displaying the “Disabled” identification sign.
A parking place within a 30-meter-long area for vehicles, except motorized wheelchairs.
A parking place within a 30-meter-long area for motorized wheelchairs and automobiles displaying the “Disabled” identification sign.
qs.x: The blue P with a wheelchair plaque and a 30 m plaque with arrows marks a 30 m parking zone for motorized wheelchairs and cars displaying the Disabled sign.

qs.q: Which of these signs is considered a vehicle identification sign?
qs.x: Sign 3, the yellow square with a red border and running children, is a vehicle identification sign; the other two are road signs.

qs.q: Traffic of which vehicles is prohibited by this traffic sign?
qs.x: The car in a red ring prohibits all motor vehicles, not just cars.

qs.q: Which sign indicates that an obstruction may be passed on either the right or the left?
qs.x: Sign 5, a blue disc with two diverging white arrows, allows passing the obstruction on either side.

qs.q: Which sign is placed on the front and rear of vehicles transporting organized groups of children?
qs.x: Sign 1, the yellow square with a red border and running children, goes on the front and rear of vehicles carrying organized groups of children.

qs.q: What do the indicated traffic signs show?
o: The priority road continues to the left at the intersection.
The priority road continues straight ahead and to the left at the intersection.
qs.x: The plaque below the yellow diamond Priority Road sign shows that at the intersection the priority road turns to the left.

qs.q: What do the indicated traffic signs show?
o: Within the area of effect of the supplemental plaque, drivers must proceed at a speed higher than the speed shown on the sign.
Within the area of effect of the supplemental plaque, drivers are advised to proceed at the speed shown on the sign.
qs.x: The blue square sign with 50 and the 800 m plaque with arrows recommend that speed on that stretch.

qs.q: Which signs apply only during the period when the roadway surface is wet?
qs.x: Only sign C carries the rain-cloud plaque, so only it applies just while the road surface is wet.

qs.q: What should the driver do in this situation?
o: Move into the part of the roadway intended for oncoming traffic.
qs.x: The yellow temporary sign shows traffic being moved over to the opposite side, so we must move into the part of the road meant for oncoming traffic.

qs.q: What do the following traffic signs indicate?
o: There is a narrowing of the road from the right 150–300 m beyond the sign, and the narrowed section is 100 m long.
There is a narrowing of the road from the right 100 m beyond the sign.
qs.x: The right-narrowing triangle with the 100 m plaque means a narrowed section 100 m long begins some 150–300 m ahead.

qs.q: In which direction is the driver permitted to proceed?
o: To the right and left only.
Straight ahead and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The red-ringed sign with the double-headed arrow plaque closes the road to both left and right, leaving only straight ahead and a U-turn.

qs.q: What do the indicated traffic signs show?
o: Stopping is prohibited on Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays.
qs.x: The no-stopping sign with the red asterisk plaque applies on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays, i.e. non-working days.

qs.q: Which traffic sign prohibits a U-turn?
qs.x: Sign 3, the crossed-out U-shaped arrow, prohibits a U-turn, while signs 1 and 2 prohibit right and left turns.

qs.q: What do these traffic signs indicate?
o: Entering the shoulder is dangerous because of roadwork.
Roadwork is being carried out on the road.
qs.x: The roadwork triangle with the plaque of a car beside the shoulder warns that driving onto the shoulder is dangerous.

qs.q: What must the driver do when the following traffic sign is installed before an intersection?
o: Proceed through the intersection while maintaining safety.
Yield to vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road.
Stop before the sign and yield to vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The red octagonal STOP sign requires a full stop before the line or sign and yielding to traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Which traffic signs do not apply to public transit vehicles?
qs.x: Only the fourth sign, the car in a red ring, does not apply to public transit vehicles, whereas the parking and stopping bans apply to them too.

qs.q: The following traffic sign indicates:
o: At the intersection, traffic must proceed to the left or to the right.
Reversible traffic is established on the intersecting road.
One-way traffic is established on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The blue square with a double-headed arrow at the intersection indicates reversible traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: In this situation, must the driver yield to the truck?

qs.q: What do the following traffic signs indicate?
o: When the road is icy, traffic must proceed at a speed of 40 km/h.
When the roadway surface is wet, the maximum permitted speed is 40 km/h.
qs.x: The red-ringed 40 with the rain-cloud plaque sets a 40 km/h maximum when the road surface is wet.

qs.q: What do the following traffic signs indicate?
qs.x: The no-stopping sign with the crossed-hammers plaque applies on working days (weekdays).

qs.q: What do the following traffic signs indicate?
o: On this section of road, the maximum permitted speed is 50 km/h.
A speed of 50 km/h is recommended on this section of road.
Driving is permitted only at the speed indicated on the sign or higher.
qs.x: The blue square with 50 is a recommended-speed sign, and the windsock triangle beside it warns of crosswinds.

qs.q: Which traffic sign requires a driver to proceed only to the left or to the right?
qs.x: Sign 3, the blue disc with arrows splitting left and right, allows only a left or right turn.

qs.q: What do the following traffic signs indicate?
o: When the roadway surface is wet, a speed of 40 km/h is recommended.
When the roadway surface is wet, the maximum permitted speed is 40 km/h.
qs.x: The blue square 40 with the rain-cloud plaque recommends that speed on a wet road.

qs.q: The effect of these traffic signs applies:
o: On the left side of the road.
On the right side of the road.
On the side of the road where they are installed.
qs.x: The odd-date and even-date parking-ban signs apply on the side of the road where they are installed.

qs.q: In this situation, along which path or paths is it permitted to go around the obstruction?
qs.x: The blue disc with two diverging arrows shows the barrier can be passed on the right (A) or on the left (B).

qs.q: What should the driver do in this situation?
o: Stop at least 5 meters before the first railroad track.
qs.x: At the crossing a red STOP sign stands in front of the crossbuck, so the driver must stop before the second sign, the STOP sign.

qs.q: What should the driver do if intending to make a right turn at the intersection?
o: The driver may change into the right traffic lane and then make the right turn.
The driver may approach the intersection and then make the right turn.
qs.x: The blue lane signs above the intersection allow a right turn from the right lane and from the straight-or-right lane, so both approaches are valid.

qs.q: In this situation, at a distance of 200 m from the sign, is the driver permitted to make a U-turn?
qs.x: The blue U-turn sign with the 200 m plaque indicates a designated place for a U-turn 200 m ahead, so turning there is permitted.

qs.q: In this case, must the driver stop at the location indicated by the traffic controller?
o: No, because the sign prohibits stopping.
qs.x: The traffic controller's signals override road signs, so you must stop where he indicates despite the no-stopping sign in the picture.

qs.q: What should the driver do in this situation?
o: Proceed through the railroad crossing while ensuring safety.
Proceed through the railroad crossing without stopping.
Stop before the sign and then, while ensuring safety, proceed through the multiple-track railroad crossing.
qs.x: The double crossbuck marks a multiple-track crossing and the red STOP sign requires stopping first, then crossing only when safe.

qs.q: What does the pavement marking on the roadway indicate?
o: The boundaries of lanes designated for vehicles proceeding in the same direction.
The boundaries of a reversible traffic lane.
qs.x: The overhead lights with a red X and a green arrow above the lane mark a reversible traffic lane.

qs.q: In which direction or directions is the passenger car permitted to proceed?
o: To the left and by making a U-turn.
Straight ahead, to the left, and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: On the sign the right-pointing arrow with the bus is reserved for transit vehicles, so a passenger car may go straight, left or make a U-turn, but not right.

qs.q: What should the driver do in this situation?
o: If necessary, yield to a vehicle proceeding on the intersecting road.
Stop and yield to a vehicle proceeding on the intersecting road.
qs.x: The red STOP sign and the stop line require a full stop and yielding to the vehicle on the intersecting road, not just yielding if necessary.

qs.q: Outside populated areas, at what distance before the beginning of a hazardous section is this warning sign installed?
qs.x: The winding-road warning triangle is placed 150–300 m before the hazard outside built-up areas.

qs.q: In which direction is traffic permitted?
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
Straight ahead, to the right, and to the left.
qs.x: The blue straight-arrow sign marks a one-way road, so straight, right and left are allowed, but not a U-turn.

qs.q: Which of the following traffic signs prohibits entering an intersection area if congestion has formed ahead in the direction of traffic, except when making a right or left turn?
qs.x: Sign 3, the grey square with a yellow border and diagonals (Intersection Area), prohibits entering the intersection if a jam has formed ahead.

qs.q: At what maximum distance may the “Intersection Area” traffic sign be installed at a complex intersection if it cannot be installed at the boundary of the intersection?
qs.x: The Intersection Area sign, the square with a yellow cross, may be placed at most 30 m away if it cannot be put at the intersection boundary.

qs.q: What does the following traffic sign warn about?
o: Entering the intersection area is prohibited if congestion has formed ahead in the direction of traffic and would force the driver to stop.
Entering the intersection area is prohibited if congestion has formed ahead in the direction of traffic.
qs.x: The square with the yellow cross forbids entering the intersection if a jam ahead would force you to stop inside it.

qs.q: What does the following pavement marking indicate?
o: A section of an intersection that may not be entered if congestion has formed ahead in the direction of traffic and would force the driver to stop.
qs.x: The yellow criss-cross grid marking denotes an intersection area you may not enter if congestion would make you stop in it.

qs.q: Which of the following pavement markings indicates a section of an intersection that may not be entered if congestion has formed ahead in the direction of traffic and would force the driver to stop?
qs.x: The yellow grid (option 3), unlike the zebra bars or the chevron wedge, marks the area you may not enter when traffic is jammed.

qs.q: Making a U-turn from the indicated lane is:
qs.x: The sign above permits only straight or right from this lane and there is a double solid line to the left, so a U-turn is prohibited.

qs.q: Along which path is it permitted to make a U-turn?
qs.x: The straight-only sign applies from where it stands, so a U-turn is allowed only along path A, made before the sign.

qs.q: Along which path is it permitted to make a U-turn?
qs.x: The signs in view (end of one-way road and the two-way traffic warning) allow a U-turn along neither path A nor B.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver may continue straight ahead through this intersection?
qs.x: The blue mandatory right-turn sign does not apply to public transit vehicles, so only the transit driver may go straight.

qs.q: Along which path is a U-turn permitted?
o: At the intersection, along path A.
Before the intersection, along path B.
qs.x: The straight-only sign applies from its location, so the U-turn at the intersection along A is allowed but not along B.

qs.q: Must you stop before the “Stop Line”?
qs.x: The traffic light is green and a signal takes precedence over the STOP sign, so there is no need to stop at the stop line.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted:
o: Only in directions A or B.
qs.x: The blue sign with straight and right arrows permits only straight (B) or right (A); left (C) is not allowed.

qs.q: This traffic sign indicates:
o: The distance from the end of the tunnel.
The distance from a location hazardous to children.
The location of an emergency exit and the distance to it.
qs.x: The green arrow sign in the tunnel with a door, a running figure and 150 m shows the emergency exit and its distance.

qs.q: In this situation:
o: We must yield to the truck driver.
We may proceed through the narrow section first.
qs.x: The blue sign with a large white up arrow and a small red down arrow gives us priority over the oncoming truck, so we may pass the narrow section first.

qs.q: After these signs, the driver of a truck with a maximum authorized mass not exceeding 3.5 metric tons may proceed at a maximum speed of:
qs.x: The plaque with a car silhouette under the 80 sign covers cars and trucks up to 3.5 t, so such a truck may travel at up to 80 km/h.

qs.q: What is prohibited by this traffic sign?
o: Proceeding at a speed greater than 20 km/h.
qs.x: The sign with a pedestrian in a blue disc and the zone wording marks a pedestrian zone, where all vehicle traffic is prohibited.

qs.q: Where must the driver stop in order to comply with the sign?
o: Before the intersection of the roadways (C).
qs.x: With a STOP sign and no stop line, you stop before the intersecting roadway (C), not at the sign or earlier.

qs.q: Which sign limits speed?
qs.x: Only sign 2, the Residential Zone sign with a car, people and houses, limits speed; yield, recommended 50 and loose-gravel signs do not.

qs.q: Which sign applies only to the lane above which it is installed?
qs.x: Sign A, the 50 limit with the down-arrow plaque, applies only to the lane above which it is installed.

qs.q: Parking at the indicated location is:
qs.x: The no-parking sign is still ahead and the car is before it at the roadside, so parking there is allowed.

qs.q: Has the truck driver violated the parking rules?
