qs.x: The plaque under the P sign allows parking only in the shown way, with wheels on the kerb parallel to the road, but the truck stands at an angle on the pavement, so it violated the rules.

qs.q: In which direction is traffic permitted?
o: Straight ahead and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The sign on the right shows a crossed-out left-turn arrow, so a left turn is banned while straight ahead and a U-turn remain allowed.

qs.q: Which sign does not apply to you if you reside within the area where the sign is in effect?
qs.x: Signs A (plain red ring) and C (car in red ring) do not apply to residents' vehicles, while B (the red disc with a white bar, No Entry) applies to everyone.

qs.q: What does the supplemental plaque indicate?
o: The distance from the sign to the intersection when a “Yield” sign is installed immediately before the intersection.
The distance from the sign to the intersection when a “STOP” sign is installed immediately before the intersection.
The location of a border checkpoint.
qs.x: The STOP 250 m plaque shows the distance to the intersection where a STOP sign is installed right before it.

qs.q: Stopping at the indicated location is:
qs.x: The no-stopping sign is still ahead of us, so stopping at our current position is allowed.

qs.q: Which signs remain in effect in the direction of traffic up to the nearest intersection?
qs.x: A and C carry the zone plaque and apply within the zone, while ordinary signs B (50) and D (no parking) apply up to the nearest intersection.

qs.q: What speed regulation is established on the road by these signs?
o: Minimum speed in the left lane proceeding in the same direction: 50 km/h.
qs.x: The blue disc 50 with a down-arrow plaque sets a minimum speed of 50 km/h only for the lane the arrow points to.

qs.q: Which of the signs prohibits making a left turn?
qs.x: Signs A (left arrow reserved for the bus) and C (U-turn) keep ordinary vehicles from turning left, while B bans only a U-turn.

qs.q: Is the driver permitted to make a left turn?
qs.x: The sign only shows a dead end on the left side road and imposes no ban, so a left turn is permitted.

qs.q: The signs indicate that:
o: Within a 150 m section of road, there is a danger of pedestrians entering the roadway.
There is an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing 150 m ahead.
qs.x: The triangle with a pedestrian on zebra stripes and the 150 m plaque warns of an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing 150 m ahead.

qs.q: Along which paths is traffic permitted?
qs.x: The blue Roundabout sign requires circulating counter-clockwise, so only path B is allowed, whereas A is cut off by the no-right-turn sign and C goes against the flow.

qs.q: Which of the signs prohibits proceeding at a speed below 40 km/h?
qs.x: The Motorway (A) and Road for Automobiles (B) signs forbid driving slower than 40 km/h, while C is only a recommended speed.

qs.q: With which sign must you yield to oncoming traffic at a narrow section?
qs.x: A shows a steep descent where the downhill driver must give way at a narrow section, and C, the red-ringed arrows sign, directly requires yielding to oncoming traffic.

qs.q: In which direction or directions may you continue through this intersection if you are driving a truck with a maximum authorized mass of 3.5 metric tons?
o: To the right, to the left, or by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The red-ringed truck sign without a weight applies to trucks over 3.5 t, so a 3.5 t truck may go in any direction.

qs.q: Is a right turn onto the unpaved road permitted?
qs.x: There is no sign banning a right turn; the triangle and chevron boards only warn about the bend, so turning right onto the unpaved road is allowed.

qs.q: Is stopping at the indicated location to pick up a passenger permitted?
qs.x: The no-parking sign (blue disc with one slash) with the 50 m plaque bans only parking, so stopping to pick up a passenger is allowed.

qs.q: Which sign indicates a pedestrian path?
qs.x: The blue disc with a walking figure (B) is the pedestrian path; A bans pedestrians and C marks a pedestrian crossing.

qs.q: This traffic sign:
o: Warns of an approaching narrow section.
Requires the driver to yield to oncoming traffic at narrow sections.
qs.x: The red circle with black and red arrows requires yielding to oncoming traffic at a narrow section, such as the oncoming truck here.

qs.q: What should you do if you need to reverse your direction of movement?
o: Make a U-turn at this intersection.
Proceed straight through the intersection and then make a U-turn.
qs.x: The blue sign mandates straight ahead only, so to reverse direction you drive straight through and make the U-turn elsewhere.

qs.q: Parking at the indicated location is:
qs.x: A no-stopping sign (red cross on blue) stands at the right, and a stopping ban also covers parking, so parking there is prohibited.

qs.q: When this supplemental plaque is used, the sign with which it is used applies to:
o: Passenger cars and trucks with a maximum authorized mass not exceeding 3.5 metric tons.
qs.x: The plaque with a black car silhouette extends the sign to passenger cars and trucks with a maximum authorized mass up to 3.5 t.

qs.q: This traffic sign indicates that:
o: Stopping on the shoulder is prohibited.
Entering the shoulder is dangerous because of roadwork.
Stopping is permitted only on the roadway.
qs.x: The roadworks triangle with the plaque of a car at the roadside means entering the shoulder is dangerous because of roadwork.

qs.q: In which direction or directions is traffic permitted from the indicated lane?
o: Straight ahead and to the left.
Straight ahead, to the left, and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The lane signs show that from the leftmost lane straight, left and a U-turn are all permitted.

qs.q: In which of the indicated directions may you continue through this intersection?
qs.x: The straight-only sign stands at the far side and applies from its location, so A and B are allowed, while the right turn (C) passes the sign.

qs.q: This traffic sign:
o: Recommends proceeding at a speed of 40 km/h.
Permits proceeding only at a speed of 40 km/h or higher.
Prohibits proceeding at a speed higher than 40 km/h.
qs.x: The red-ringed 40 prohibits driving faster than 40 km/h.

qs.q: Which supplemental plaques indicate the area of effect of the sign with which they are used?
qs.x: Plaques B (arrows and 100 m) and C (arrow and 10 m) show the zone of effect, while A (300 m) gives only a distance ahead.

qs.q: Which yard is the driver permitted to enter?
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign governs the intersection itself and does not ban entering a yard; the right yard, beyond the intersection, may be entered.

qs.q: Which sign takes effect immediately from the location where it is installed?
qs.x: A's plate with arrows gives a zone starting at the sign and B has no plate, so both act immediately; C's 200 m plate is a distance ahead to the hazard.

qs.q: Along which path is it permitted to continue?
qs.x: The U-turn sign allows turning around, and going straight or along C and D is fine; only path B does not follow the permitted manoeuvre.

qs.q: What does this traffic sign warn about?
o: An approaching slippery section of road.
An approaching wet and dirty section of road.
An approaching section of road where loose gravel may be thrown up by vehicle tires.
qs.x: The triangle shows a car with stones flying from its wheels, which is the loose-gravel warning sign.

qs.q: Within the area of effect of which sign do the traffic rules applicable in populated areas not apply?
qs.x: The blue sign (C) marks a settlement where built-up-area rules do not apply, while the white signs (A, B) introduce those rules.

qs.q: In which direction or directions is the passenger-car driver permitted to proceed in this situation?
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign with a truck plate applies only to trucks, so a passenger car may go in any direction.

qs.q: Unloading an automobile within the area where this traffic sign is in effect is:
o: Permitted if it takes no more than 5 minutes.
qs.x: The no-parking sign bans only parking; stopping to load or unload is allowed regardless of how long it takes.

qs.q: Which of the signs prohibits a U-turn?
qs.x: These are only direction-of-traffic information signs (one-way, bus lane); none of them prohibits a U-turn.

qs.q: Is it permitted to enter the indicated yard?
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign applies to the intersection and does not prevent entering adjacent territory such as a yard.

qs.q: In this situation, stopping to pick up a passenger is:
qs.x: The no-stopping sign with a double-headed arrow plate applies on both sides of the sign, so picking up a passenger is prohibited both before and after it.

qs.q: After which signs is proceeding prohibited without permission?
qs.x: Only the Customs (B) and Danger (C) signs, with red rim and bar, forbid proceeding without permission.

qs.q: What is the minimum distance from the location of this sign at which an intersection of roads of equal priority may be encountered?
qs.x: In a populated area, warning signs are placed at least 50 m before the hazard.

qs.q: In which of the directions indicated by the arrows may towing continue?
qs.x: The no-trailers sign also covers towing another vehicle, so path B past the sign is closed and only A may be used.

qs.q: From what point do the requirements regulating traffic in a populated area take effect?
o: After the “Beginning of Populated Area” sign with a white background.
Only after signs with a white or blue background that contain the name of the populated area.
Only after the beginning of the developed area.
qs.x: Built-up-area rules take effect from the white-background Beginning of Populated Area sign.

qs.q: This traffic sign:
o: Warns of an intersection with tram tracks.
Warns of an approaching tram stop.
Requires yielding to the tram operator.
qs.x: The triangle shows a tram, so this is the warning sign for a crossing with tram tracks.

qs.q: These signs require you to maintain between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead:
o: A distance of up to 70 m over a 900 m section of road.
A distance of at least 70 m over a 900 m section of road.
A distance of 70 m after proceeding 900 m.
qs.x: The distance sign with the 900 m plate and arrows requires at least 70 m behind the vehicle ahead along that 900 m stretch.

qs.q: In which direction or directions may you continue from the indicated lane?
o: To the left and straight ahead.
To the left, straight ahead, and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The sign above the middle lane allows a left turn and straight ahead; a U-turn is not provided for.

qs.q: These signs warn that:
o: There is a three-track railroad crossing ahead.
There is a railroad crossing without a barrier gate 150–300 m ahead.
There is a railroad crossing 50–100 m ahead.
qs.x: The plate with three red stripes means a railroad crossing without a barrier lies 150–300 m ahead.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
o: Permitted only for residents of the indicated area.
qs.x: The sign acts only from its position in the direction of the arrow, and the spot is before the sign, so parking is allowed.

qs.q: Which sign requires the driver of a 5-metric-ton truck to make a right turn at the intersection?
qs.x: Only the round blue turn-right sign B is mandatory; A and C are rectangular information signs.

qs.q: In which direction or directions may you continue through the indicated intersection if you are driving a truck with a maximum authorized mass of 3 metric tons?
o: Straight ahead and to the right only.
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign with the truck plate applies to trucks over 3.5 t, so a 3 t truck may go in any direction.

qs.q: In this situation, the horn may be used:
o: Only to warn of an intention to pass.
Only when necessary to prevent a traffic accident.
In both of the listed cases.
qs.x: Under the no-horn sign, the horn may be used only to prevent a traffic accident.

qs.q: Which sign is used to mark a speed hump?
qs.x: A speed hump is marked by the blue square sign A; B and C are triangular warning signs.

qs.q: Along which path may you continue?
qs.x: A right turn must end in the nearest right-hand lane, which path A does, while B ends in the far lane.

qs.q: At an uncontrolled intersection, which signs give the driver the right-of-way over vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road?
qs.x: Sign A (priority road) and C (side road junction) give priority over traffic on the intersecting road.

qs.q: Is passing permitted in this situation?

qs.x: The no-overtaking sign does not apply to two-wheeled motorcycles, so passing is allowed.

qs.q: Has the truck driver violated the parking rules?
o: Yes, if the maximum authorized mass exceeds 3.5 metric tons.
qs.x: The sidewalk-parking plate shows a passenger car, so the truck driver has violated the parking rules.

qs.q: Along which path is the U-turn permitted?

qs.q: On odd-numbered dates of the month, is parking permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The odd-date no-parking sign applies until 7:00 PM, after which the sides switch, so parking is allowed after 7:00 PM.

qs.q: Which signs indicate the section where drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the roadway?
qs.x: Signs B (pedestrian crossing) and C (residential zone) mark places where drivers must yield to pedestrians; A only warns.

qs.q: Which sign warns that you are approaching the beginning of a road with two-way traffic?
qs.x: Only the triangular warning sign A warns of the start of two-way traffic; B and C are information signs.

qs.q: Are you permitted to enter your workplace located within the area where these signs are in effect?
qs.x: The signs restrict through traffic; a person who works or lives within the zone may enter on any day, whatever the plate says.

qs.q: Is a passenger car towing a trailer permitted to proceed straight ahead through the intersection?
o: Permitted only for persons residing within the area where the sign is in effect.
qs.x: The no-trailers sign takes effect only from where it stands, not at the intersection before it, so going straight through is allowed.

qs.q: In which of the indicated directions is traffic permitted?
qs.x: The sign shows the cross street is one-way to the left, so straight (A), left (B) and a U-turn (C) are all allowed; only a right turn is impossible.

qs.q: This sign:
o: Indicates the directions of traffic at the intersection.
qs.x: The sign with red-and-white chevrons shows the directions of travel at a T-intersection and prohibits nothing.

qs.q: Which sign indicates the length of the lane provided for making a U-turn?
qs.x: Sign B gives the length of the U-turn lane (15 m), while A's plate gives the distance to the U-turn place.

qs.q: At what minimum distance from the sign will a slippery section of road begin in a populated area?
qs.x: In a populated area, warning signs stand at least 50 m before the hazard.

qs.q: Which vehicles are not subject to the “No Stopping” sign in this situation?
o: Only motorized wheelchairs and automobiles displaying the “Disabled” identification sign.
qs.x: The crossed-out wheelchair plate exempts only vehicles displaying the Disabled sign; taxis are not exempt.

qs.q: At the next intersection, in which of the indicated directions may you continue?
qs.x: The straight-ahead sign governs the previous intersection; at the next one, every direction is allowed.

qs.q: Within the area of effect of which sign may you proceed at a speed of 60 km/h?
qs.x: A caps speed at 50, B sets a minimum of 50, and C only recommends 50, so 60 km/h is fine under B and C.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the parking rules?
o: The motorcycle operator and the passenger-car driver.
qs.x: The parking sign with the plate covers cars and motorcycles, and the truck stands before the sign outside its zone, so nobody has violated the rules.

qs.q: Which of the indicated directions is permitted?
qs.x: The no-right-turn sign rules out D, and path B does not follow the proper movement, leaving the left turn (A) and straight ahead (C).

qs.q: When used with which supplemental plaque does the sign apply to the driver of a truck with a maximum authorized mass of less than 3.5 metric tons?
qs.x: Plates with a passenger car (B and C) extend the sign to trucks under 3.5 t, while A applies to heavier trucks.

qs.q: Which case indicates a railroad crossing with two or more tracks?
qs.x: A crossing with two or more tracks is shown only by the double-cross sign C; A and B are single-track warnings.

qs.q: A U-turn along the indicated path is:
qs.x: A U-turn in front of the roundabout would mean driving against its circulation, so it is prohibited.

qs.q: Parking beyond the overpass is:

qs.q: These traffic signs indicate:
o: An approaching railroad crossing with a barrier gate.
A railroad crossing without a barrier gate.
qs.x: The sign showing a barrier gate warns of an approaching railroad crossing with a barrier.

qs.q: Which signs permit a U-turn?

qs.q: From the indicated lane, traffic is permitted:

qs.x: The sign over the leftmost lane allows a left turn, and a U-turn from that lane is also allowed since nothing prohibits it.

qs.q: This sign indicates that you are approaching a tunnel:
qs.x: The triangle with a tunnel warns of a tunnel with no artificial lighting.

o: Stopping is prohibited at all of the indicated locations.
qs.x: The no-stopping sign acts from its location onward, so stopping is allowed only before it, at B.

qs.q: With which sign may you make a left turn?
qs.x: A left turn is possible with B (dead-end information sign) and C (counter-flow bus lane); A marks one-way traffic to the right.

qs.q: This sign gives advance warning of:
o: The need to yield to bicyclists.
An intersection with a bicycle path.
qs.x: The triangle with a bicycle warns of an intersection with a bicycle path.

qs.q: Which vehicle drivers are subject to these signs?
qs.x: The parking sign with a car-on-sidewalk plate applies to passenger cars and motorcycles.

qs.q: Under which sign, after stopping, may you not resume proceeding without permission?

qs.q: The vehicles will proceed through the intersection in the following order:
o: The passenger car, the bus, then the trolleybus.
The trolleybus and the bus, then the passenger car.
The trolleybus, the passenger car, then the bus.
qs.x: By the main-road plate, the trolleybus is on the main road and goes first, then the car, while the bus yields to both.

qs.q: Which vehicle will proceed through the intersection first?

qs.x: The blue car has the red car on its right, which in turn has the truck on its right, so blue yields to both and goes last.

qs.q: The blue automobile will proceed through the intersection:
qs.x: The light is green and the red car turning left must yield to the oncoming blue car going straight, so blue goes first.

qs.q: Which answer correctly states the order in which the vehicles will proceed through the intersection?
o: The bus, the passenger car, the bicycle.
The passenger car, the bus, the bicycle.
The bicycle, the bus, the passenger car.
qs.x: Nothing is on the bicyclist's right, the bus has the bicyclist on its right, and the car has the bus on its right: bicycle, bus, car.

qs.q: Which vehicle will proceed through the intersection second?
qs.x: The blue car turning left yields to both the oncoming red car and the tram; the tram goes second, after the red car.

qs.q: In which direction is traffic prohibited?
o: To the right through the first passage.
To the right through the second passage.
To the right through the first and second passages.
qs.x: The no-right-turn sign stands at the second passage, so a right turn is prohibited there, not at the first.

o: The bus driver and the motorcycle operator.
The passenger-car driver and the truck driver.
qs.x: The controller's right arm is stretched forward: the car on his left side may go in all directions, the truck and bus on his right side and back only turn right, and the motorcycle facing his chest must stop.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield?
qs.x: The car has a green light while the tram has red with a green right arrow, so the tram turning right must give way to the car going on green.

qs.q: If the traffic controller’s right arm is extended forward, traffic of non-rail vehicles is permitted:
o: From the left side, to the left and by making a U-turn.
From the right side, to the right only.
From the left side, in all directions.
From the rear, to the right only.
qs.x: With the controller's right arm extended forward, traffic from his left side may go in all directions.

qs.q: The vehicles will proceed through the intersection in the following order:
o: The tram and the bus, then the passenger car.
The tram, the passenger car, the bus.
The passenger car, then the tram and the bus.
qs.x: The car has the main green light and goes first, while the tram and bus, on red with only a green arrow, must give way to it.

qs.q: Which answer correctly identifies the vehicle or vehicles permitted to proceed?
o: The passenger car and the truck.
qs.x: From the controller's stance only the red passenger car's side may move, while the motorcycle, truck and bus are on prohibited sides.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield?
qs.x: The motorcycle has a green light while the car has red with a green right arrow, so the car turning right must yield to the motorcycle.

qs.q: This signal given by the traffic controller means that traffic is permitted for:
o: The blue and green automobiles; traffic is prohibited for the red, yellow, and white automobiles.
The blue, red, and green automobiles; traffic is prohibited for the yellow and white automobiles.
qs.x: With arms spread the controller allows traffic from his sides, so the blue, red and green vehicles may go while the yellow and white face his chest or back and stop.

qs.q: Which vehicles may make a right turn?
qs.x: The controller has his arms spread, so the red and green cars on his sides may go straight or turn right, while those facing his chest or back must stop.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted:
o: To the right through the first passage.
To the right through the second passage.
To the right through the first and second passages.
qs.x: The controller's right arm is stretched forward, so from his right side or back only a right turn is allowed; the red car may only turn right at the first opening.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted:
o: To the right through the first passage.
Straight ahead and to the right through the first passage.
qs.x: With the controller's right arm stretched forward, the red car on that side may only turn right at the first opening, not go straight.

qs.q: If the traffic controller’s arms are extended to the sides or lowered, traffic of non-rail vehicles is permitted:
o: From the front and rear, to the right only.
From the left and right sides, straight ahead and to the right.
From the left and right sides, straight ahead only.
qs.x: With the controller's arms lowered or out to the sides, traffic from his left and right may go straight or right.

qs.q: The driver of the red automobile:
qs.x: The red car faces a red light with only a green straight arrow, so it must give way to traffic from other directions, here the green estate car.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to proceed?
o: The green, red, and white automobiles.
qs.x: The controller has his arms spread: the yellow and red cars at his sides may go, while the blue, green and white at his chest or back may not.

qs.q: Under which traffic signal may the automobile driver complete the U-turn?
qs.x: The car is waiting at the second stop line (marked STOP), so it may complete the U-turn only on the green signal.

qs.q: What does the combination of yellow and red traffic signals mean?
o: Traffic is prohibited, and the signals indicate that the green signal will turn on shortly.
A vehicle with a special audible signal and flashing beacons activated is approaching the intersection.
qs.x: Red and yellow lit together prohibit movement and warn that the green signal is about to come on.

qs.q: In which image is the driver making the turn correctly?
qs.x: In the left image the driver follows the controller's signal, while in the right image the controller's arm position does not allow that turn.

qs.q: When the traffic signal is green, must the tram operator yield to vehicles approaching from other directions?
qs.x: With the main light red, the green arrow only allows the turn, and the tram operator must give way to vehicles from other directions.

qs.q: This traffic signal is used to regulate traffic:
o: Across the entire width of the roadway.
In roadway lanes where the direction of traffic may change to the opposite direction.
Only in lanes designated for public transit vehicles.
qs.x: The red cross and green arrow form a reversible-lane signal, which regulates lanes where the direction of traffic can be switched.

qs.q: If the traffic controller’s right arm is extended forward, traffic of non-rail vehicles from the controller’s left side is permitted:
qs.x: With his right arm forward, traffic from the controller's left may go in all directions.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to proceed under this traffic signal?
o: The tram, the yellow automobile, and the red automobile.
qs.x: The green arrows allow straight and right only, so the yellow car in the middle lane and the red car in the right lane may go, but the blue car and the tram on the left may not.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted for:
qs.x: The motorcycle is at the side of the controller whose arms are spread and may go, while the car and tram facing his chest must stop.

qs.q: If the traffic controller’s arms are extended to the sides or lowered, traffic of non-rail vehicles from the controller’s left and right sides is permitted:
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: With his arms out or lowered, traffic from his left and right may go straight or right.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver has the right-of-way?
qs.x: The tram has a green signal, and a tram on rails has priority over the car, so the tram goes first.

qs.q: Traffic is prohibited for:
o: The white, blue, and green automobiles.
qs.x: The controller has his arms spread: the blue, green and white cars at his chest or back are prohibited, while the red and yellow may proceed.

qs.q: When this traffic signal is red, traffic is prohibited:
o: Across the entire width of the roadway.
At a speed not exceeding 50 km/h.
In the lane over which the signal is located.
qs.x: The red cross prohibits traffic only in the lane over which the signal is mounted, not across the whole roadway.

qs.q: What is the meaning of the circular flashing green traffic signal?
o: It indicates that entering the intersection is prohibited.
It permits traffic and indicates that its display period is ending and a prohibitory signal will be activated shortly.
qs.x: A flashing green permits movement and warns that a prohibiting signal will come on shortly.

qs.q: The vehicles will proceed through the intersection in the following order:
o: The tram, the red automobile, the green automobile.
The red automobile, then the tram simultaneously with the green automobile.
The tram simultaneously with the green automobile, then the red automobile.
qs.x: The red car with its green signal goes first, while the tram and green car, on red with only a green straight arrow, must wait and then go together.

qs.q: Which answer correctly identifies the vehicles that are permitted to proceed?
qs.x: The controller's right arm is stretched forward: from his left side cars and the motorcycle may go in all directions, while the tram may only turn left, not go straight.

qs.q: If the traffic controller’s right arm is extended forward, traffic of non-rail vehicles from the controller’s left side is permitted:
o: Straight ahead and to the left.
qs.x: With his right arm forward, traffic from his left may proceed in all directions.

qs.q: Traffic is prohibited for:
o: The blue-and-yellow automobile when proceeding to the left.
The blue-and-yellow automobile when proceeding straight ahead, and the red automobile when proceeding straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: The controller's arms are lowered, so traffic from the sides may go straight or right; only the blue-and-yellow car's left turn is prohibited.

qs.q: In which direction is traffic permitted?
o: Straight ahead and to the right through the first passage.
To the right through the first passage.
To the right through the second passage.
To the right through the first and second passages.
qs.x: With the main light red and only the green right arrow lit, only a right turn at the first opening is allowed.

qs.q: Which vehicle will proceed through the intersection first?
qs.x: The green truck has a green light while the red and blue cars are on red with only a right arrow, so the green truck goes first.

qs.q: In which image is the driver making the turn correctly?
qs.x: In the left image the driver follows the controller's signal, while in the right image the controller's arm position does not allow that turn.

qs.q: The red automobile will proceed through the intersection:
qs.x: The red car turning left on green must give way to the oncoming green and yellow cars and the tram, so it goes last.

qs.q: The automobile will proceed through the intersection:
qs.x: The blue car has a green light while the tram is on red with only a right arrow and must yield, so the car goes first.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted for:
o: The blue-and-yellow automobile straight ahead, and the red automobile to the right.
The red automobile straight ahead and to the right, and the blue-and-yellow automobile straight ahead.
qs.x: The controller's arms are lowered, so the red car may go straight and right and the blue-and-yellow car straight, as the arrows show.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted for:
o: The tram and the red automobile.
qs.x: From the controller's arm position only the red car's side may move, while the motorcycle, tram and truck are on prohibited sides.

qs.q: Is it permitted to proceed along the indicated path when the reversible traffic signals are off?
o: Permitted for the purpose of passing.
Permitted if there are no oncoming vehicles.
qs.x: When the reversible-lane signals are off, entering the left lane along the arrow shown is prohibited because oncoming traffic may use it.

qs.q: In this situation, which vehicles are permitted to continue?
o: The passenger car straight ahead, the patrol vehicle in all directions, and the bus to the right only.
Only the patrol vehicle, in all directions.
The patrol vehicle in all directions and the bus to the right only.
qs.x: The controller's signals override the traffic light: with his right arm stretched forward the bus may only turn right, while the patrol car with its beacon and siren may go in all directions.

qs.q: What does the traffic signal indicate?
o: When proceeding through the intersection, drivers must follow the requirements of the traffic sign.
Drivers must wait for a permissive traffic signal.
qs.x: The red-plus-yellow combination means green is about to come on, so the driver must wait for the permissive signal.

qs.q: Is the passenger-car driver permitted to pass the bus when the reversible traffic signal is off?
o: Permitted if the bus is moving at 30 km/h.
Permitted if there are no oncoming vehicles.
qs.x: With the reversible-lane signals off, moving into the oncoming lane to pass the bus is prohibited because oncoming traffic may be there.

qs.q: Which vehicle must yield?
o: The motorcycle and the passenger car.
qs.x: The bus under the Yield sign must give way to the motorcycle and the car going straight on the main road.

qs.q: The following drivers are permitted to continue along the indicated paths:
o: The bus driver and the truck driver.
The passenger-car driver and the bus driver.
qs.x: The controller's arms are lowered: only the bus at his side turning right may go, while the truck and the U-turning taxi face his chest or back and must stop.

qs.q: The vehicles will proceed through the intersection in the following order:
o: The tram, the passenger car, the bus.
The passenger car, the tram, the bus.
The passenger car, the bus, the tram.
qs.x: The car goes straight first on green, while the tram and bus, on red with a green right arrow, yield, and the tram has priority over the bus.

qs.q: In which direction may the driver continue?
o: To the right through the first passage.
To the right through the first and second passages.
To the left through the first passage.
qs.x: With the main light red and only the green right arrow lit, only a right turn at the first opening is allowed.

qs.q: When making a right turn, the driver must yield to:
o: The driver may continue without stopping.
qs.x: Turning right, even on green, we must yield to both the pedestrians on the crossing and the cyclist riding straight past the bicycle-path sign.

qs.q: The vehicles will proceed through the intersection in the following order:
o: The tram, the bus, the truck, the motorcycle.
The bus, the truck, the tram, the motorcycle.
The bus, then the tram and the motorcycle, then the truck.
qs.x: The bus goes first, then the tram and the motorcycle, which do not interfere, go together, and the truck, crossing the tram tracks, goes last.

qs.q: In this situation, to which tram operator must you yield?
qs.x: Although our signal is green, our path crosses the tram tracks and a tram on rails has priority, so we must yield to both trams A and B.

qs.q: Which driver has the right-of-way?
qs.x: The bus is stopped by the signal for its direction while the car proceeds on a permissive light, so the car has the right-of-way.

qs.q: In this situation, when making a left turn:
o: I will yield to the tram.
I will proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: The green left arrow lets us turn while the tram's white horizontal lights stop it, so we go first.

qs.q: What should you do in this situation?
o: Enter the intersection and, after yielding to the passenger-car driver, proceed through the intersection.
Wait before the “Stop Line” until the passenger-car driver has proceeded through the intersection.
qs.x: On green, turning left we enter the intersection, give way to the oncoming car going straight, then complete the turn.

qs.q: Which driver violates the traffic rules when making the turn?
qs.x: Both are in straight-only lanes (blue arrow signs), so turning right from them breaks the rules despite the right arrow.

qs.q: In this situation, when making a right turn, must you yield?
qs.x: With a red light the green right arrow only permits the turn, and we must still yield to traffic from other directions, here the car on the right.

qs.q: Is a right turn permitted in this situation?
o: Yes, provided you do not interfere with pedestrians.
qs.x: The controller's signal permits the right turn, but we must not hinder the pedestrians on the crossing.

qs.q: In this situation, must you yield to the tram operator?
qs.x: Our path crosses the tram tracks and the tram on rails has priority over a car, so we must yield.

qs.q: When the green traffic signal turns on, the driver:
o: Must yield to the truck driver.
qs.x: When green comes on we must let vehicles still clearing the intersection finish, so we yield to the truck that is still crossing.

qs.q: At this intersection, the driver:
qs.x: The tram signal stops the tram with white lights while our signal permits movement, so we go first.

qs.q: When proceeding straight through the intersection, the driver:
qs.x: Even with our light green, the tram crossing the intersection on its rails has priority, so going straight we must yield to it.

qs.q: When making the turn, the driver must yield to:
qs.x: Turning right, even on green, we must yield to both the pedestrians on the crossing and the cyclist on the bicycle path.

qs.q: When making a right turn, must you yield to the driver approaching in the oncoming lane?
qs.x: Turning right we enter the right-hand lane while the oncoming car stays in its own, so there is no need to yield to it.

qs.q: When proceeding straight through the intersection:
o: We must yield to the passenger-car driver.
qs.x: Our light is red with only a straight green arrow, so we must yield to the blue car on the left, which is crossing on green.

qs.q: When making a left turn, you must yield to:
o: The passenger-car driver and the pedestrians.
qs.x: Turning left on green, we must yield to the oncoming car going straight and to the pedestrians crossing the road we enter.

qs.q: In this situation, is a right turn permitted?
o: Yes, provided you do not interfere with the pedestrian.
qs.x: The controller's signal allows the right turn, but we must not hinder the pedestrians on the crossing.

qs.q: When making a left turn:
o: You must yield to the tram operator.
You will proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: Turning left we cross the tram tracks, and the tram on rails has priority, so we yield to it.

qs.q: Which traffic signs do not apply when their requirements conflict with traffic signal indications?
qs.x: Priority signs do not apply when they conflict with traffic signals; the signals govern.

qs.q: In this situation, who must yield?
qs.x: The tram has a red light with only a green arrow, so it must give way to the car proceeding on green.

qs.q: When making a right turn:
o: We must yield to the tram operator.
We will proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: The controller's signal lets us turn right while the tram on the other side is held back, so we go first.

qs.q: You intend to make a left turn. To whom must you yield?
o: The automobile driver and the tram operator.
qs.x: Turning left on green, we must give way to both the oncoming car going straight and the tram.

qs.q: When making a left turn:
o: I will complete the maneuver without stopping.
After entering the intersection, I will stop before the second “Stop Line” and wait for the green signal.
qs.x: There is a second stop line with a red signal ahead, so after entering we stop before the second line and wait for green.

qs.q: In this situation, must we yield to the truck driver?
qs.x: Turning left on green, we must still give way to the oncoming truck going straight.

qs.q: In this situation, when making a left turn, you must:
o: Enter the intersection and wait for the traffic controller’s signal permitting a left turn.
Stop before the “Stop Line” pavement marking and wait for the traffic controller’s signal permitting a left turn.
Enter the intersection and, after yielding to the driver approaching in the oncoming lane, proceed through the intersection.
qs.x: The traffic light is dark and the controller directs traffic, so to turn left we stop before the stop line and wait for his permissive signal.

qs.q: In which case may you proceed through the intersection without yielding to another road user?
qs.x: Going straight on green we yield to no one, whereas turning requires giving way to pedestrians or oncoming vehicles.

qs.q: When making a right turn, you must:
o: Stop before the “Stop Line” so as not to interfere with pedestrians.
Enter the intersection and stop so as not to interfere with pedestrians.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.
qs.x: Turning right on green, pedestrians and a cyclist cross the road we enter, so we move into the intersection and stop so as not to hinder them.

qs.q: When making a right turn:
o: You must yield to the passenger-car driver.
You will proceed through the intersection first.
qs.x: The controller's signal permits our right turn and the car on the right by the U-turn marking does not hinder us, so we go first.

qs.q: After the permissive traffic signal turns on, we may enter the intersection:
o: Only when making a turn or a U-turn.
qs.x: There is a queue ahead, so going straight we would get stuck and block the intersection, while entering to turn or make a U-turn is acceptable on green.

qs.q: When the green traffic signal turns on, we must:
o: Make sure that there are no pedestrians who have not finished crossing in the part of the pedestrian crossing that is not visible.
Immediately start moving in accordance with the traffic signal.
qs.x: The truck blocks part of the crossing, so when green comes on we must check that no pedestrians are still crossing in the hidden part.

qs.q: In this situation, when making a left turn, you must yield to:
o: The bus driver and the pedestrian.
qs.x: Turning left on green, we must yield to the oncoming bus and to the pedestrians crossing the road we enter.

qs.q: Must you yield to the bus?
qs.x: Our light is red with a green right arrow while the bus on the left has green, so turning right we must give way to the bus.

qs.q: In this situation, when making a U-turn, must you yield to the other driver?
qs.x: In a U-turn we must give way to traffic the controller lets move, here the blue car coming from the left.

qs.q: In which direction or directions may the driver continue in this situation?
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
Straight ahead and to the left.
qs.x: The controller's arm lets us continue only straight, and the blue arrow sign on the right shows that street is one-way against us, so no right turn.

qs.q: Which driver may continue?
qs.x: The controller's signal overrides the red light, and his outstretched arm allows movement from the side where both the minibus and the car stand.

qs.q: Proceeding across the railroad crossing is:
qs.x: The flashing white-lunar light at the crossing permits movement, so crossing the railroad is allowed.

qs.q: The driver is:
o: Prohibited from proceeding through the intersection.
Permitted to proceed through the intersection in all cases.
Permitted to proceed through the intersection if the driver cannot stop before the “Stop Line” without sudden braking.
qs.x: The controller's raised arm means stop, but a driver who cannot stop before the stop line without sudden braking may proceed.

qs.q: When complying with the traffic signal, where must the driver stop?
qs.x: There is no stop line or crossing, and the STOP plate is on the signal itself, so on red we stop before the traffic signal.

qs.q: A left turn is permitted:
o: From the lane indicated in the image.
qs.x: A left turn is allowed from the lane shown in the picture; the reversible lane is closed by the X above it and cannot be used.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted:
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: The traffic controller faces us side-on with arms lowered, so driving straight and to the right is allowed.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted:
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: Our lane carries only a right-turn arrow, so only a right turn is allowed from it.

qs.q: The arrows shown in the green traffic signal indicate that:
o: Traffic to the right is controlled by an additional traffic-signal section.
qs.x: An arrow shown on the green signal means traffic in that direction is controlled by an additional signal section.

qs.q: Is passing the truck permitted?
qs.x: A red X is lit above our lane, so entering the reversible lane and passing are prohibited.

qs.q: In which direction or directions may the driver continue in this situation?
o: The driver must wait for a permissive signal.
To the left and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: From the left lane, a green left arrow permits both a left turn and a U-turn.

qs.q: In this situation, entering the reversible traffic lane is:
o: Permitted only for the purpose of passing.
qs.x: A green arrow is lit above our lane, so driving in this reversible lane is permitted.

qs.q: Proceeding straight ahead from the indicated lane is:
o: Permitted only after the main green signal turns on.
qs.x: Only a right arrow is lit in the extra section while the main signal is red, so going straight is prohibited.

qs.q: Traffic is permitted:
o: Straight ahead and to the right.
qs.x: The controller faces us chest-on with the right arm extended forward, so all directions are allowed.

qs.q: In this situation, traffic is:
qs.x: The controller has his back to us with the arm extended, so traffic from our side is prohibited.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to park?
o: The passenger car and the motorcycle.
qs.x: The No Parking sign has a truck plate, so the ban applies only to trucks; the car and motorcycle may park.

qs.q: Parking is prohibited:
o: On bridges, elevated roadways, and overpasses.
Under bridges, elevated roadways, and overpasses.
In all of the listed cases.
qs.x: Parking is prohibited both on and under bridges, elevated roadways and overpasses.

qs.q: Is it permitted to drop off a passenger at a location where a solid yellow line is marked on the upper surface of the curb and a “No Stopping” sign is posted?
o: Permitted if no public transit vehicles are present.
Permitted only for public transit vehicles.
qs.x: The solid yellow curb line and the No Stopping sign ban stopping, so dropping off a passenger is banned too.

qs.q: Does the prohibitory sign apply to the section of road where the driver has stopped?
qs.x: A prohibitory sign applies up to the nearest intersection; the U-turn pocket and sign do not cancel it.

qs.q: Is parking the automobile at the indicated location permitted?
qs.x: There is no prohibiting sign or marking here, so parking at the right edge of the road is permitted.

qs.q: Within what distance of a railroad crossing is parking prohibited?
qs.x: Parking is prohibited within 25 m of a railroad crossing.

qs.q: In this situation, is stopping to drop off a passenger permitted?
o: Permitted if it does not interfere with the movement of public transit vehicles.
qs.x: In the public-transit lane, stopping to drop off a passenger is allowed if it does not hinder transit vehicles.

qs.q: Which driver is required to stop?
qs.x: The bus has stopped at the crossing for a pedestrian, so the passenger-car driver must stop.

qs.q: This pavement marking permits traffic:
o: To the left and by making a U-turn.
Straight ahead, to the left, and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The lane arrow shows a left turn, and from the leftmost lane a U-turn is also permitted.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to park within the area where this traffic sign is in effect?
o: Vehicles driven by persons with disabilities and taxis with the taximeter activated.
qs.x: The No Parking sign does not apply to vehicles driven by disabled persons or to taxis with the meter running.

qs.q: What does this pavement marking indicate?
o: A place for picking up and dropping off passengers.
A public transit vehicle stop and taxi parking area.
qs.x: The yellow zigzag marking beside the stop sign marks a public transit vehicle stop.

qs.q: What does the solid yellow horizontal pavement marking indicate?
o: A location where stopping and parking of vehicles are prohibited.
A location where stopping is permitted to drop off passengers or unload the vehicle.
A location where parking of vehicles is prohibited.
qs.x: A solid yellow line at the roadway edge or on the curb prohibits both stopping and parking.

qs.q: Is the driver permitted to cross the solid pavement marking that indicates the boundaries of vehicle parking spaces?
qs.x: A solid line marking parking-space boundaries does not regulate traffic, so it may be crossed.

qs.q: In which direction or directions indicated by the arrows is traffic permitted?
o: To the left and by making a U-turn.
Straight ahead, to the left, and by making a U-turn.
qs.x: The line to the left of our lane may not be crossed, so a left turn or U-turn is impossible; only straight is allowed.

qs.q: What does this pavement marking indicate?
o: A pedestrian crossing where traffic is controlled by a traffic signal.
A location where a bicycle path crosses the roadway.
A location where a pedestrian path crosses the roadway.
qs.x: The row of squares across the road marks where a bicycle path crosses the roadway.

qs.q: How many lanes does a road have when traffic flows in opposite directions are separated by double solid lines?
qs.x: A double solid line separates opposing traffic on roads with four or more lanes.

qs.q: What do the arrows marked on the roadway warn about?
o: They warn the driver of an approaching hazardous section of road.
They warn of an approaching end of the traffic lane.
They indicate the direction of a hazardous turn in the road.
qs.x: The slanted arrows on the roadway warn that the traffic lane is about to end.

qs.q: Which of these pavement-marking lines is used to designate lanes with reversible traffic?
qs.x: Reversible lanes are marked by line 2, the double broken line.

qs.q: Where is the solid yellow line indicating locations where stopping and parking are prohibited marked?
o: Near the edge of the roadway.
Near the edge of the roadway or on the upper surface of the curb.
Only on the upper surface of the curb.
qs.x: The solid yellow no-stopping line is drawn near the roadway edge or on top of the curb.

qs.q: With which traffic sign may a broken yellow pavement marking be used?
o: “No Parking on Odd-Numbered Days of the Month.”
qs.x: A broken yellow line goes with the No Parking sign: it bans parking only, not stopping.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to proceed in the right lane of the roadway?
qs.x: The right lane is set off by a solid line and marked A, so it is for public transit vehicles only.

qs.q: This pavement marking has the following meaning:
o: It indicates curbside parking spaces where the positioning of motor vehicles is specified.
It indicates locations where stopping of motor vehicles is prohibited.
It indicates public transit vehicle stops and taxi parking areas.
qs.x: The yellow zigzag marking shows public transit stops and taxi parking places.

qs.q: This horizontal pavement marking indicates:
o: A narrowing of the roadway where the number of traffic lanes in the given direction decreases.
A location where the driver must stop, if necessary, to yield to vehicles proceeding on the intersecting road.
An approach to a location where stopping is prohibited.
qs.x: The row of triangles (give-way line) marks where you must stop if necessary to yield to traffic on the crossing road.

qs.q: Is it permitted to enter a channelizing island marked with wide white lines?
qs.x: Entering a channelizing island marked with wide white lines (chevrons) is prohibited.

qs.q: What should the driver do when approaching an intersection with a “Stop Line” pavement marking and a green traffic signal?
o: Stop at the “Stop Line” and then resume driving.
Proceed through the intersection without stopping.
qs.x: The stop line applies only at a red signal or STOP sign; on green you drive through without stopping.

qs.q: What does this pavement marking indicate?
o: A location where a bicycle path crosses the roadway.
A location designated for driving livestock across the road.
qs.x: The row of squares across the road shows where a bicycle path crosses the roadway.

qs.q: Where must the driver stop the vehicle when this pavement marking is present?
o: At least 5 m before the pavement marking.
qs.x: At the give-way line the driver stops right at the marking without crossing it.

qs.q: What does this pavement marking mean?
o: A traffic lane designated for public transit vehicles.
A traffic lane designated for special-purpose vehicles.
It indicates the boundaries of traffic lanes where reversible traffic control is in effect.
qs.x: The double broken line marks the boundaries of lanes under reversible traffic control.

qs.q: Is it permitted to make a U-turn at the indicated location?
qs.x: The line on our side of the double marking is broken, so a U-turn is permitted here.

qs.q: When this pavement marking is present, is the driver of a bus operating on a tourist route permitted to enter the lane marked “A”?
qs.x: A bus on a tourist route counts as a route vehicle, so it may enter the lane marked A.

qs.q: What does the wide broken-line pavement marking indicate?
o: The boundary between the roadway and the shoulder.
The boundary between a main traffic lane of the roadway and an acceleration lane.
The boundary between a main traffic lane of the roadway and a deceleration lane.
qs.x: The wide broken line separates the main lane from the acceleration lane.

qs.q: Which automobile is permitted to stop within the area where these signs are in effect?
o: The yellow automobile displaying the “Disabled” identification sign.
qs.x: The No Stopping sign does not apply to the yellow car bearing the Disabled badge; the red car may not stop.

qs.q: In which image has the driver stopped correctly to drop off passengers?
qs.x: In the left image the car stops at least 5 m from the intersection; in the right it stands on the pedestrian crossing.

qs.q: The signal to stop a train is:
o: A circular motion of the arm (during daylight, with a brightly colored cloth or another clearly visible object; at night, with a torch or lantern).
An arm raised above the head holding a disk or red flag.
An arm extended forward and moved up and down.
qs.x: The signal to stop a train is a circular motion of the arm (a bright cloth by day, a lantern at night).

qs.q: In populated areas, on roads with one traffic lane in each direction and no tram tracks in the center, stopping and parking on the left side of the road are:
qs.x: In a populated area, on a road with one lane each way and no tram tracks, stopping and parking on the left are permitted.

qs.q: At what distance from the “Stop Line” or the “STOP” sign must a vehicle be stopped in order to yield to an approaching train?
o: Immediately at the “Stop Line” and/or the sign.
qs.x: To yield to a train, stop immediately at the stop line and/or sign.

qs.q: Is stopping at the indicated location permitted?
qs.x: The car is at the solid yellow curb line, which prohibits stopping.

qs.q: Is the automobile permitted to stop at this location?
o: Prohibited because the distance between the broken pavement marking and the stopped vehicle is less than 3 m.
Prohibited on even-numbered days of the month.
qs.x: The sign bans only parking, not stopping, and there is no solid line, so stopping is permitted.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver has violated the parking rules?
o: The driver of the blue automobile.
The driver of the red automobile.
Both drivers have violated the rules.
Neither driver has violated the rules.
qs.x: The blue car parks in the No Parking zone and the red one in a forbidden spot, so both violate the rules.

qs.q: Outside populated areas, where is parking for extended rest, overnight stays, or other purposes permitted?
o: On the shoulders of the road.
In areas designated for parking or outside the boundaries of the road.
On the right side of the roadway, provided it does not interfere with other vehicle traffic.
On the left side of the road, provided road traffic safety is ensured.
qs.x: Outside populated areas, long-term parking is allowed only in designated parking areas or off the road.

qs.q: Stopping is prohibited if the distance between the solid line and the stopped vehicle is:
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited if less than 3 m remains between the solid line and the stopped vehicle, i.e. 2.5 m here.

qs.q: If traffic across a railroad crossing is prohibited and there are no traffic signals, traffic signs, pavement markings, or barrier gate, the driver must stop:
o: At least 5 m from the nearest rail.
At least 7 m from the nearest rail.
At least 10 m from the nearest rail.
qs.x: With the crossing closed and no gate, signal or signs, stop at least 10 m from the nearest rail.

qs.q: Within what distance of a railroad crossing is vehicle parking prohibited?
qs.x: Parking is prohibited within 15 m of a railroad crossing.

qs.q: Which answer correctly identifies the drivers who have violated the stopping rules?
o: The drivers of the red automobile and the motorcycle.
The driver of the blue automobile.
The drivers of all the vehicles.
qs.x: The No Stopping sign with a double-arrow plate covers both sides of the road, so all drivers violated it.

qs.q: Which vehicle drivers have stopped incorrectly to drop off passengers?
o: The motorcycle operator and the bus driver.
qs.x: The motorcycle stands on the pedestrian crossing and the minibus within 5 m of it, while the red car stopped correctly.

qs.q: If traffic across a railroad crossing is prohibited and there are no traffic signals, traffic signs, or pavement markings, the driver must stop:
o: At least 5 m before the barrier gate.
At least 3 m before the barrier gate.
qs.x: With the crossing closed, stop at least 5 m before the barrier gate.

qs.q: What does the letter “A” marked in a traffic lane of the roadway mean?
o: A special lane designated for public transit vehicles.
A special lane designated for category A vehicles.
qs.x: The letter A on a lane marks a special lane for public transit vehicles.

qs.q: Is the vehicle permitted to stop at the indicated location to drop off passengers?
o: Permitted, but only by driving onto the sidewalk.
qs.x: The solid yellow curb line prohibits stopping, even to drop off a passenger, and driving onto the sidewalk is not allowed.

qs.q: Is it permitted to continue in the direction indicated by the arrow?
o: Permitted for the purpose of stopping to drop off passengers.
Permitted for the purpose of passing the truck.
qs.x: Moving in the direction of the arrow is allowed only to stop and drop off a passenger.

qs.q: This type of vertical pavement marking indicates:
o: The lower edges of a bridge or tunnel.
The entrance to an unlit tunnel.
Any element of a road structure that creates a hazard for traffic.
qs.x: This black-and-white vertical marking indicates the lower edges and supports of bridges and tunnels.

qs.q: What should the passenger-car driver do if the bus driver has begun braking?
o: Reduce speed, stop if necessary, and continue after making sure there are no pedestrians in the crossing.
Stop and continue only after the bus resumes driving.
qs.x: The braking bus signals a pedestrian, so slow down, stop if necessary, and continue only when the crossing is clear.

qs.q: The bus driver has stopped to pick up passengers. The passenger car is proceeding at a speed of 70 km/h. Which vehicle driver is violating the requirements of the traffic rules?
qs.x: The bus stopped properly at the right edge and 70 km/h does not exceed the permitted speed.

qs.q: Where must the driver stop in this situation?
o: Before the intersection of the traffic lanes.
qs.x: At the red light you stop before the stop line, not at the signal or beyond it.

qs.q: The bus has stopped to yield to a pedestrian. In this situation, is the passenger-car driver violating the requirements of the traffic rules?
qs.x: The bus has stopped for a pedestrian, and the car overtakes it at the crossing, which is a violation.

qs.q: Where must the bus driver stop in order to yield to the passenger car before continuing to the left?
o: At a safe location at the driver’s discretion.
qs.x: The bus driver must stop at the give-way marking (triangles) to yield to the car.

qs.q: Where must the driver stop in this situation?
qs.x: At a STOP sign the driver must stop before the stop line.

qs.q: Which vehicles are permitted to stop within the area where this sign is in effect?
o: Only vehicles driven by persons with disabilities.
Only taxis with the taximeter activated.
Stopping is prohibited for all vehicles.
qs.x: The No Stopping sign prohibits stopping for all vehicles without exception.

qs.q: Within the area where these traffic signs are in effect, is stopping to pick up passengers permitted?
qs.x: The No Parking sign bans only parking, so stopping to pick up a passenger is permitted.

qs.q: For which vehicles is the lane marked with the letter “A” designated?
o: Only buses operating on an established route.
qs.x: The lane marked A is reserved for public transit vehicles.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Stopping at the right edge is permitted because no sign or marking prohibits it.

qs.q: Is parking permitted in this situation?
qs.x: Parking on the carriageway beside the barrier, with no shoulder and limited visibility, is prohibited.

qs.q: At which of the indicated locations is stopping permitted?
qs.x: Stopping on a crossing or within 5 m before it is prohibited, so only B, beyond the crossing, is allowed.

qs.q: At which location is stopping permitted?
qs.x: A is at the left edge of a one-way street and B is before the sign, while C is inside the No Stopping zone, so A and B are allowed.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
o: Only for the purpose of picking up a passenger.
qs.x: Stopping on the yellow zigzag marking is prohibited because that space is for public transit vehicles.

qs.q: In the indicated situation, is stopping permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger?
qs.x: Stopping in a tunnel is prohibited, including to pick up a passenger.

qs.q: In which of the indicated cases is stopping permitted?
qs.x: A and C are on or just before the crossing, while B is beyond it, so only B is allowed.

qs.q: Stopping is prohibited:
o: At a railroad crossing and within 50 m of it.
At a railroad crossing and within 50 m before it.
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited at the crossing itself; near it only parking is banned.

qs.q: Parking is prohibited:
o: At a railroad crossing and within 50 m of it.
At a railroad crossing and within 50 m before it.
qs.x: Parking is prohibited at the crossing and within 50 m of it.

qs.q: Which option shows a vehicle stopped correctly?
qs.x: Only C has stopped at the right edge of the road; A and B stand on the carriageway or the left side.

qs.q: Must you yield to the truck?
qs.x: The obstruction (the broken-down car) is on the truck's side, so the truck must yield to us.

qs.q: Stopping at the indicated location is:
qs.x: The car is at the right edge, more than 3 m from the solid line and clear of the crossing, so stopping is permitted.

qs.q: When is it permitted to cross the pavement marking?
qs.x: The line is solid up to the pedestrian crossing and may be crossed only after it, where it becomes broken.

qs.q: Has the truck driver violated the stopping rules?
qs.x: The truck driver has stopped on the sidewalk, and stopping on the sidewalk is prohibited.

qs.q: In the indicated situation, is stopping permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger?
o: Permitted only for the driver of a public transit vehicle.
qs.x: At the stop sign and zigzag marking only the driver of a public transit vehicle may pick up passengers.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the parking rules?
o: Only the driver of the motorcycle.
qs.x: The car is parked on the sidewalk, while the motorcycle stands properly at the roadway edge.

qs.q: Which option shows a driver parked in a prohibited position?
qs.x: Car A is parked at an angle to the edge, whereas B is parallel to the edge, the permitted position.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
o: Only for the purpose of dropping off a passenger.
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited on the crossing and within 15 m of the bus stop, even to drop off a passenger.

qs.q: At which of the indicated locations is parking permitted?
qs.x: A and C are outside the No Parking sign zone, while B is under it, so parking is allowed at A or C.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited within 5 m of the intersecting road, and the indicated spot is closer than that.

qs.q: Who has violated the stopping rules?
qs.x: The truck stands closer to the intersection than allowed, while the car keeps the required 5 m.

qs.q: In which case has the driver violated the stopping rules?
o: Both drivers have violated the rules.
qs.x: Stopping is banned only at the crossing itself, and both cars are well away from it, so neither violates the stopping rules.

qs.q: In which case has the driver violated the parking rules?
o: Both drivers have violated the rules.
qs.x: Both cars are parked within 50 m of the crossing, where parking is prohibited.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The No Parking sign with a Zone plate prohibits parking throughout the whole zone.

qs.q: Is stopping on the bridge permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger?
qs.x: Stopping on a bridge is prohibited, including to pick up a passenger.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the stopping rules?
qs.x: Outside a populated area the car stands on the left side and the motorcycle on the carriageway, so both violate the rules.

qs.q: Which driver has stopped correctly?
qs.x: Outside populated areas you stop on the right shoulder, and only C does; A and B are on the left.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: Less than 3 m would remain between the solid line and the car (the road is 4 m wide), so stopping is prohibited.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the parking rules?
qs.x: The parking sign allows parking only in the indicated manner; the passenger car does not follow it and so violates the rule.

qs.q: Is the driver of a truck weighing less than 3.5 metric tons permitted to park in the manner indicated on the supplemental plaque?
qs.x: The plate shows a passenger car with wheels on the sidewalk, so that manner of parking is not allowed for a truck under 3.5 t.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The car would stop closer than 5 m to the intersecting road, which is prohibited.

qs.q: At which of the indicated locations is stopping permitted?
qs.x: The No Parking sign does not ban stopping, so only A is allowed; B stands in the middle of the carriageway.

qs.q: Parking at the indicated location is:
qs.x: The car is 15 m from the bus stop sign, outside the restricted zone, so parking is permitted.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the parking rules?
qs.x: The plate dictates how to park; B does not follow it while A parks correctly.

qs.q: Stopping at the indicated location is:
o: Permitted for the purpose of picking up a passenger.
qs.x: Stopping is prohibited within 5 m of a pedestrian crossing, and the car stands too close.

qs.q: Which driver has violated the stopping rules?
qs.x: A stopped on the right shoulder, while B and C stand on the carriageway, so B and C violate the rules.

qs.q: Are the drivers permitted to stop at the indicated location?
o: Only the driver of the motorcycle.
qs.x: Less than 3 m would remain to the solid line, so stopping is prohibited for everyone, motorcycle included.

qs.q: In which of the indicated cases is stopping permitted?
qs.x: In a populated area on a one-lane-each-way street stopping is allowed at both edges, so it is permitted in all cases.

qs.q: Is stopping in this position permitted?
qs.x: The car stands not parallel to the edge but sticking out into the road, which is not allowed.

qs.q: Stopping at the indicated location is:
o: Permitted if the distance from the vehicle to the pavement marking is more than 3 meters.
qs.x: On this narrow street less than 3 m would remain to the solid line, so stopping is prohibited.

qs.q: This pavement marking indicates:
o: Approach to a curved section of road.
Approach to the end of the lane.
qs.x: The curved slanted arrows show the approach to the end of the lane.

qs.q: What does this pavement marking indicate?
o: Approach to the “Stop Line” at a signal-controlled intersection.
Approach to the “Stop Line” pavement marking when it is used together with a “STOP” sign.
qs.x: The word STOP on the road warns of an approaching stop line used together with the STOP sign.

qs.q: Vertical markings on barriers indicate:
o: Movement along a dangerous section of road.
qs.x: The black-and-white vertical marking on barriers warns of travel along a dangerous section of road.

qs.q: This triangular pavement marking indicates:
o: Approach to a location where drivers must yield.
Approach to a location where vehicles must stop.
qs.x: A triangle painted on the road announces the approach to a place where you must give way.

qs.q: These broken pavement markings within the intersection indicate:
qs.x: Broken lines inside an intersection show the traffic lanes.

qs.q: With this pavement marking, passing is:
qs.x: The line on our side is broken, so passing the slow tractor is permitted.

qs.q: This vertical pavement marking:
o: Marks all vertical elements adjacent to the roadway.
Marks only those elements of road structures that present a hazard to drivers.
qs.x: Vertical marking is applied only to road-structure elements that pose a hazard to traffic.

qs.q: With this pavement marking, may you enter the intersection if doing so does not interfere with the passenger-car driver?
qs.x: The give-way triangles and sign require yielding to traffic on the crossing road, so entering is not allowed.

qs.q: Which driver following the indicated path does not violate the pavement-marking requirements?
qs.x: Path A crosses the solid line while path B crosses a broken section, so only B obeys the marking.

qs.q: In which case is it permitted to cross the solid pavement marking?
qs.x: A solid line may be crossed only to stop where stopping is allowed, which applies only to B.

qs.q: What does the broken pavement marking indicate?
o: The right to stop on the shoulder.
The edges of the roadway on a two-lane road.
The right to proceed on the shoulder.
qs.x: The broken line on a two-lane road marks the edges of the roadway.

qs.q: In this situation, proceeding along this path is:
qs.x: The path crosses the double solid line toward lanes under crossed-out signals, so it is prohibited.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
o: Permitted without driving onto the sidewalk.
qs.x: The solid yellow curb line bans stopping and parking, so parking here is prohibited.

qs.q: With this pavement marking, passing is:
o: Permitted if the vehicle ahead is a slow-moving vehicle.
qs.x: The line on our side is solid, so passing is prohibited even though the vehicle ahead is slow.

qs.q: May you continue beyond the sign?
qs.x: The STOP sign stands before the stop line, so you may proceed past the sign up to the stop line.

qs.q: When orange and white pavement markings conflict, drivers:
o: May follow whichever pavement marking is more convenient.
Must follow the white pavement marking.
Must follow the orange pavement marking.
qs.x: Orange marking is temporary, so when it conflicts with white marking the orange one is followed.

qs.q: Which driver is permitted to cross the solid pavement marking when stopping?
o: The driver proceeding from the opposite direction.
qs.x: Only the oncoming driver, on whose side there is a permitted stopping place, may cross the solid line to stop.

qs.q: Is stopping permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The broken yellow line bans only parking, so stopping is permitted.

qs.q: This pavement marking:
o: Indicates the boundaries of a Residential Zone.
qs.x: The row of black-and-white squares across the road marks a speed hump.

qs.q: This pavement marking prohibits:
o: Traffic to the left of it or over it.
qs.x: The solid edge line prohibits driving beyond it or on it, outside the roadway.

qs.q: This pavement marking indicates:
o: The maximum permitted speed on the indicated road section.
qs.x: The number in the circle painted on the road is the maximum permitted speed for that section.

qs.q: The marking applied to the roadway indicates:
o: The distance from the nearest intersection.
The distance from the nearest populated area.
qs.x: The inscription A 100 on the roadway is the road or route number.

qs.q: On which side may the obstruction be passed?
qs.x: The arrow on the roadwork sign directs passing only on the left, side A.

qs.q: Which vehicles may use the rightmost lane of this road?
qs.x: The right lane carries the letter A and a bus sign, so it is for trolleybuses and public transit buses.

qs.q: Is parking permitted at the indicated location?
qs.x: The broken yellow line at the curb prohibits parking, although stopping is allowed.

qs.q: The increasing length of the broken pavement-marking segments indicates:
o: Approach to the end of the lane.
Approach to a dangerous road section.
That the pavement marking will soon become a solid line.
qs.x: Lengthening dashes warn that the broken line will soon become a solid line.

qs.q: In the indicated situation, proceeding straight ahead is:
o: Permitted after changing to the right lane.
qs.x: The left lane has only a left arrow, so to go straight you must change into the right lane.

qs.q: How many traffic lanes does this road have?
qs.x: A double solid line splits the road into two directions with two lanes each, four in total.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for passenger cars on roads outside populated areas?
qs.x: Outside populated areas, passenger cars may drive at most 90 km/h.

qs.q: Trucks carrying people in an equipped cargo bed are permitted to proceed at a speed not exceeding:
qs.x: A truck carrying people in an equipped cargo bed must not exceed 60 km/h.

qs.q: Vehicles transporting organized groups of children are permitted to proceed at a speed not exceeding:
qs.x: Vehicles carrying organized groups of children are limited to 60 km/h.

qs.q: In populated areas, vehicles are permitted to proceed at a speed not exceeding:
qs.x: The general maximum speed in populated areas is 60 km/h.

qs.q: At what speed are trucks with a maximum authorized mass not exceeding 3.5 metric tons permitted to proceed outside populated areas?
qs.x: Outside populated areas, trucks up to 3.5 t may drive up to 90 km/h, like passenger cars.

qs.q: During towing, if the hazard warning lights are absent or malfunctioning, the emergency warning triangle must be placed:
o: At the rear of the towed vehicle.
At the front of the towing vehicle.
On either vehicle, in a visible location, at the driver’s discretion.
qs.x: Without working hazard lights, the warning triangle goes at the rear of the towed vehicle, where following drivers can see it.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid coupling, the distance between the vehicles must not exceed:
qs.x: With a rigid coupling the gap between the vehicles must not exceed 4 m.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, is it permitted to carry people in the cargo bed of a truck?
o: Permitted in the cargo beds of both the towing and towed trucks.
Permitted only in the cargo bed of the towed truck.
Permitted only in the cargo bed of the towing truck.
Prohibited in the cargo beds of both trucks.
qs.x: While towing, people may ride only in the towing truck's bed, never in the bed of the towed truck.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid or flexible coupling, in which of the following cases is carrying people in the towed vehicle permitted?
o: In the cargo bed of a truck when towing with a rigid coupling.
qs.x: People may ride in a towed passenger car, but not in a towed bus or a truck bed.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing with a motor vehicle?
qs.x: When towing a motor vehicle the speed limit is 50 km/h.

qs.q: Under icy road conditions, towing is prohibited:
qs.x: On icy roads, towing with a flexible coupling is prohibited because the towed car can slide into the tow vehicle.

qs.q: What is the maximum speed at which towing may be performed under the indicated conditions?
qs.x: The 80 sign in the picture does not override the towing rule: maximum 50 km/h when towing a motor vehicle.

qs.q: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, is carrying people in the towed motor vehicle permitted?
o: Permitted in a bus and trolleybus.
Permitted only in a passenger car.
Permitted in the cargo bed of a truck and in a passenger car.
Permitted in the cab of a truck and in a passenger car.
qs.x: In a towed motor vehicle, people may ride only in a truck cab or a passenger car.

qs.q: Under icy road conditions, towing:
o: Is permitted when towing with a rigid coupling or by the partial-loading method.
qs.x: On ice, towing is allowed only with a rigid coupling or by partial loading, not with a flexible one.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing a vehicle with a flexible coupling?
qs.x: Towing with a flexible coupling is allowed at up to 50 km/h.

qs.q: In which case is towing prohibited?
o: Under icy road conditions with a rigid coupling.
Under icy road conditions with a flexible coupling.
qs.x: In icy conditions towing is prohibited with a flexible coupling, while a rigid one is allowed.

qs.q: When towing motor vehicles outside populated areas, the speed must not exceed:
qs.x: Even outside populated areas, towing a motor vehicle is limited to 50 km/h.

qs.q: Is towing motorcycles permitted?
o: Towing motorcycles with sidecars is permitted.
Towing motorcycles without sidecars is permitted.
qs.x: Towing is allowed for motorcycles with sidecars; two-wheeled motorcycles without one are unstable and may not be towed.

qs.q: When towing, what distance between the vehicles must be maintained by a flexible coupling?
qs.x: A flexible coupling must keep the vehicles 4 to 6 m apart.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed on freeways for passenger cars towing a trailer?
qs.x: A passenger car towing a trailer is limited to 90 km/h on a freeway, lower than without a trailer.

qs.q: When towing with a rigid coupling, the distance between the vehicles must not exceed:
qs.x: With a rigid coupling the distance between the vehicles must not exceed 4 m.

qs.q: When towing a motor vehicle by the partial-loading method, carrying passengers is permitted:
o: In the cargo bed of the towing vehicle.
In the cab of the towed vehicle.
In the cargo bed of the towed vehicle.
In the cab of the towing vehicle.
qs.x: With partial-loading towing, passengers may ride only in the cab of the towing vehicle.

qs.q: Is towing motorcycles with sidecars permitted?
o: Permitted only with a rigid coupling.
qs.x: Motorcycles with sidecars are stable, so towing them is permitted.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed when towing with a flexible coupling?
qs.x: The maximum speed when towing with a flexible coupling is 50 km/h.

qs.q: Cargo must be positioned and, when necessary, secured on the vehicle so that it:
o: Does not extend above the sides of the cargo bed.
Does not create significant noise, raise dust, or pollute the road or the environment.
Does not extend more than 0.8 m beyond the rear edge of the vehicle.
qs.x: Cargo must be placed and secured so it makes no significant noise, raises no dust and does not pollute the road or environment.

qs.q: Children may be carried in the front seat of a passenger car that is not equipped with a child restraint system if they have reached the age of:
qs.x: Without a child restraint, children may sit in the front seat only from age 12.

qs.q: Is carrying people in a cargo trailer permitted?
o: Permitted only for persons accompanying the cargo.
qs.x: Carrying people in a cargo trailer is prohibited, even those accompanying the cargo.

qs.q: Is carrying children under 12 years of age on the rear seat of a motorcycle permitted?
qs.x: Carrying children under 12 on the rear seat of a motorcycle is prohibited.

qs.q: While the vehicle is moving, are persons permitted to be in the cargo bed of a truck if it is not equipped for carrying people?
o: Permitted on roads that are not freeways.
Permitted only for persons accompanying the cargo or proceeding to receive it, provided they are seated on seats installed below the level of the sides of the cargo bed.
qs.x: In an unequipped cargo bed only people accompanying or going to collect the cargo may ride, seated below the level of the sides.

qs.q: Carrying people in a cargo trailer is:
o: Permitted only for persons accompanying the cargo.
qs.x: Carrying people in a cargo trailer is prohibited.

qs.q: When towing with a flexible or rigid coupling, is carrying people in the towed motor vehicle permitted?
o: Permitted in a bus and trolleybus.
Permitted in the cab of a truck and in a passenger car.
