Permitted in the cargo bed of a truck and in a passenger car.
qs.x: In a towed motor vehicle people may ride only in a truck cab or passenger car, not in a bed or bus.

qs.q: What is the maximum speed permitted for a motorcycle in areas designated by the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” signs?
qs.x: In a residential zone all vehicles, motorcycles included, are limited to 20 km/h.

qs.q: When carrying people in an equipped cargo bed, the truck driver must proceed at a speed not exceeding:
qs.x: A truck driver carrying people in an equipped cargo bed must not exceed 60 km/h.

qs.q: During towing, the towed vehicle must have the following activated:
qs.x: The towed vehicle must have its hazard lights on so others notice the tow.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for vehicles within areas where the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” traffic signs apply?
qs.x: Within the Residential Zone signs the limit is 20 km/h.

qs.q: What is the maximum permitted speed for the driver of a truck with a maximum authorized mass not exceeding 3.5 metric tons within the area of effect of these signs?
qs.x: The truck plate under the 50 sign applies only to trucks over 3.5 t, so a truck up to 3.5 t follows the normal 90 km/h limit outside towns.

qs.q: When towing a motor vehicle, in which lane may you continue on this road?
qs.x: The sign reserves the right lane for vehicles going 60 km/h or less, and a towing vehicle is limited to 50 km/h, so it must stay in the right lane.

qs.q: What conditions must a driver take into account when selecting a speed within the permitted limits?
o: The condition of the road surface.
Visibility in the direction of movement.
qs.x: A driver must take into account both the road surface condition and the visibility ahead when choosing speed.

qs.q: Within the permitted limits, what maximum speed should a driver select?
o: A speed that ensures full control of the vehicle.
The driver may select any speed that does not exceed the maximum permitted speed.
qs.x: The driver should choose a speed that keeps full control of the vehicle; the legal maximum is not a target.

qs.q: A driver is prohibited from:
o: Exceeding the maximum speed specified by the technical characteristics of the vehicle.
Exceeding the speed specified by the “Speed Limit” identification sign displayed on the vehicle.
Driving at an unnecessarily low speed and thereby impeding the movement of other vehicles.
Braking suddenly unless necessary to prevent a traffic accident.
qs.x: All listed actions are prohibited: exceeding the vehicle's or sign's speed, needlessly slow driving and unnecessary hard braking.

qs.q: Which sign limits speed?
qs.x: The residential zone sign (2) limits speed to 20 km/h; the blue square 50 is only a recommended speed, and signs 1 and 4 set no limit.

qs.q: A driver is prohibited from:
o: Crossing a railroad crossing at a speed greater than 30 km/h.
Crossing a railroad crossing at a speed below 30 km/h.
Proceeding across a railroad crossing, without the permission of the head of the railroad track section, in slow-moving vehicles with a speed below 8 km/h or in tractors coupled to sledges.
qs.x: Without the track-section head's permission it is prohibited to cross a railroad crossing in machines slower than 8 km/h or tractors towing harrows.

qs.q: When approaching an intersection, the driver must operate the vehicle at a speed that:
o: Does not exceed the maximum permitted speed established for that road section.
Allows the driver to stop and yield to vehicles having the right-of-way.
qs.x: Approaching an intersection, speed must allow you to stop and yield to those with priority, not merely stay under the limit.

qs.q: A driver is prohibited from increasing speed:
o: If doing so would prevent a driver who is passing from completing the passing maneuver.
If doing so is necessary to clear the way for a driver who has stopped in order to yield.
If doing so is necessary to clear the intersection.
qs.x: Speeding up is prohibited when it would stop a driver who is passing you from completing the maneuver.

qs.q: A driver must reduce speed:
o: When approaching a vehicle displaying the “Transportation of Children” identification sign while children are boarding or exiting.
When an obstruction or danger to traffic arises.

When approaching a vehicle displaying flashing blue and red beacons and using a special audible signal, as well as when approaching a stationary vehicle displaying flashing blue or flashing blue and red beacons.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: Speed must be reduced in all the listed cases: children boarding, dazzle, hazards and special vehicles with beacons.

qs.q: If cargo protrudes 0.5 m beyond the side of the vehicle, measured from the outer edge of the marker light, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
qs.x: Cargo sticking out more than 0.4 m beside the marker light must be marked, so at 0.5 m marking is required.

qs.q: A truck whose driver holds a driver’s license for Categories B and C, and which meets the requirements for transporting people in a truck, may carry up to:
qs.x: A truck meeting the people-carrying requirements may carry up to 8 passengers.

qs.q: It is prohibited to transport children under 12 years of age:
o: In the cargo bed of a truck with sideboards.
In the enclosed cargo body of a truck.
qs.x: Children under 12 may not ride in the open bed of a sideboard truck; the enclosed van body is not what the ban covers.

qs.q: If cargo protrudes 1.2 m beyond the rear end of the vehicle, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
qs.x: Cargo protruding more than 1 m at the rear must be marked with the Oversized Cargo sign and lights, so at 1.2 m it is required.

qs.q: Transportation of cargo is prohibited if the cargo:
o: Restricts the driver’s field of vision.
Makes the vehicle difficult to control or reduces its stability.
Obscures exterior lights or reflectors, license plates, or identification signs, or prevents hand signals from being seen.
In all of the above cases.
qs.x: Carrying cargo is prohibited in all listed cases: it blocks vision, harms control, or covers lights and plates.

qs.q: If the condition or placement of the cargo does not allow it to be transported in compliance with the rules, the driver must:
o: Deliver the cargo safely to the nearest unloading location.
Correct the violations or stop proceeding.
qs.x: If cargo cannot be carried within the rules, the driver must fix the violations or stop driving, not just continue to the unloading point.

qs.q: If cargo protrudes 0.6 m beyond the rear end of the vehicle, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
qs.x: Rear cargo needs marking only when it protrudes more than 1 m, so 0.6 m needs none.

qs.q: If cargo protrudes 0.3 m beyond the side of the vehicle, measured from the outer edge of the marker light, must it be marked during daylight hours with the “Oversized Cargo” identification sign and, at night or under conditions of insufficient visibility, additionally with a white light or reflector at the front and a red light or reflector at the rear?
qs.x: Side cargo is marked only when it extends more than 0.4 m beyond the marker light, so 0.3 m needs none.

qs.q: When approaching a stopped vehicle with a flashing red beacon switched on, drivers of vehicles proceeding in that direction must:
o: Stop and continue only after receiving permission.
Reduce speed so that they can stop immediately if necessary.
qs.x: A flashing red beacon means the road is blocked: stop and continue only after receiving permission.

qs.q: When a vehicle with a flashing blue beacon and a special audible signal activated is approaching, drivers of vehicles must:
o: Yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
Reduce speed and yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
qs.x: A vehicle with a blue beacon and siren must be given way so it can pass unobstructed.

qs.q: Is it mandatory to have the low-beam headlights switched on during daylight hours on mopeds?
qs.x: Mopeds must run low beams in daylight, just like motorcycles.

qs.q: In which case do the rules not require a warning signal to be given?
o: Before stopping at the edge of the roadway.
Before a curve in the road within the area of effect of a “Dangerous Turn” sign.
Before changing to an adjacent traffic lane.
qs.x: Following a curve under a Dangerous Turn sign is not a maneuver, so no signal is required.

qs.q: Before changing lanes, a warning signal must be given:
o: In advance, before beginning the maneuver.
qs.x: The signal before changing lanes is given in advance, before the maneuver starts, so others can react.

qs.q: When performing a maneuver, a warning signal must be given:
o: Before changing the direction of traffic.
While changing the direction of traffic.
In advance, before changing the direction of traffic.
qs.x: A warning signal is given in advance, before changing direction.

qs.q: A warning signal given by hand must be discontinued:
qs.x: A hand signal is stopped just before the maneuver begins, so both hands are back on the wheel.

qs.q: In which case must the driver give a warning signal before stopping?
o: If another vehicle is proceeding behind the driver.
qs.x: You must signal before stopping in all cases, whether or not another vehicle is behind you.

qs.q: If forced to stop on a railroad crossing, what general alarm signal must the driver give by repeated horn signals?
qs.x: When forced to stop on a crossing, the general alarm is one long and three short horn signals.

qs.q: If a turn signal is absent or malfunctioning, a warning signal given by hand must be discontinued:
qs.x: The hand signal ends right before the maneuver begins so the driver controls the wheel.

qs.q: The following combination of horn signals constitutes the general alarm signal given at a railroad crossing:
qs.x: The general alarm at a crossing is one long and three short horn blasts.

qs.q: In which image is the driver giving a left-turn signal?
qs.x: In image 1 the red car's driver holds the left arm straight out to the side, the left-turn signal.

qs.q: When approaching a stationary vehicle with a red flashing beacon activated, drivers proceeding in the same direction must:
o: Stop and continue only after receiving permission.
Reduce speed so that they can stop immediately if necessary.
qs.x: At a flashing red beacon drivers must stop and proceed only with permission.

qs.q: For what purpose are orange or yellow flashing beacons installed on vehicles?
o: To obtain right-of-way over other road users.
To warn other road users of danger.
qs.x: Orange or yellow flashing beacons warn of danger and give no priority.

qs.q: When a vehicle with a blue flashing beacon and a special audible signal activated is approaching, drivers must:
o: Yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
Reduce speed and yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
qs.x: Yield to a vehicle with a blue beacon and siren to let it pass unobstructed.

qs.q: The blue automobile will proceed through the intersection:
o: First, simultaneously with the red automobile.
Second, simultaneously with the red automobile.
Third, simultaneously with the red automobile.
qs.x: The emergency vehicle goes first, then the green car, and the blue and red cars from the minor road go last, together.

qs.q: When a vehicle with blue and red flashing beacons and a special audible signal activated is approaching, drivers must:
o: Yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle.
Reduce speed and yield to ensure the unobstructed passage of that vehicle and the vehicles it is escorting.
qs.x: For a vehicle with blue-and-red beacons and siren, slow down and give way to it and the vehicles it escorts.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver has the right-of-way?
o: The driver of the road-cleaning vehicle.
qs.x: The road-cleaning vehicle's yellow beacon gives no priority, so the passenger car has the right of way.

qs.q: The black automobile will proceed through the intersection:
qs.x: The fire truck with signals goes first, then the black car on the main road, with the green car yielding.

qs.q: Which vehicle driver must yield?
qs.x: Even on a green light the passenger car must yield to the ambulance with beacon and siren.

qs.q: The blue automobile will proceed through the intersection:
qs.x: The special-signal car goes first, and the blue car must yield to all the others and goes last.

qs.q: Does an activated yellow (orange) flashing beacon give a vehicle the right-of-way?
qs.x: A yellow or orange flashing beacon only warns and gives no right-of-way.

qs.q: The driver of a vehicle with white flashing beacons activated gives a special audible signal in order to:
o: Obtain right-of-way over other road users.
Attract the attention of police officers and other persons.
qs.x: With white flashing beacons the siren only attracts the attention of police and others; it gives no priority.

qs.q: The driver of a vehicle equipped with a blue flashing beacon has the right-of-way over other road users if the driver:
o: Is giving a special audible signal.
Has activated the blue flashing beacon and the special audible signal.
qs.x: Priority exists only when both the blue beacon and the special siren are on together.

qs.q: Within what distance before a railroad crossing is passing prohibited?
qs.x: Passing is prohibited within 100 m before a railroad crossing.

qs.q: Is passing vehicles at an intersection permitted when proceeding on a road that is the priority road relative to the intersecting road?
qs.x: Passing at an intersection is prohibited even when on the priority road.

qs.q: Is the passenger-car driver permitted to pass in the indicated situation?
o: Permitted if the motorcycle’s speed does not exceed 30 km/h.
qs.x: Passing is prohibited: the motorcycle ahead is itself overtaking the truck, and the speed of the passed vehicle does not lift the ban.

qs.q: Passing is prohibited:
qs.x: Passing is banned at intersections; before railroad crossings the ban is 100 m, not 150 m.

qs.q: Passing is prohibited:
qs.x: Passing is prohibited at both controlled and uncontrolled intersections.

qs.q: Is it permitted to pass the road train in this situation if its speed does not exceed 30 km/h?
qs.x: The picture shows an intersection of equal roads, where passing is banned regardless of the road train's speed.

qs.q: Is the driver of the green automobile permitted to pass?
o: Permitted if the red automobile is proceeding at a speed below 30 km/h.
qs.x: Passing is prohibited, and the red car going under 30 km/h does not make it allowed.

qs.q: Is the driver of the red automobile permitted to pass in this situation?
o: Permitted if the speed of the automobile being passed does not exceed 30 km/h.
qs.x: The red car is at an intersection, where passing is prohibited; the other car's speed does not matter.

qs.q: Is it permitted to pass the bus at the indicated location?
qs.x: The crossing warning signs show the crossing is still more than 100 m away, so passing is allowed.

qs.q: Passing vehicles means:
o: Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving the occupied lane and entering the oncoming traffic lane.
Proceeding ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving the occupied lane.
qs.x: Passing is getting ahead of one or more moving vehicles by leaving your lane; entering the oncoming lane is not required.

qs.q: At night and under conditions of insufficient visibility, regardless of road lighting, moving motor vehicles must have the following activated:
qs.x: At night or in poor visibility either high or low beam may be used, depending on the situation.

qs.q: In which case must a motorcycle have its low-beam headlights activated during daylight?
o: When proceeding under conditions of insufficient visibility.
When proceeding to a parking location on a motorcycle with a malfunction.
In all cases while participating in traffic.
qs.x: A motorcycle must have its low beam on whenever it is in traffic, even in daylight.

qs.q: What must the driver do first if dazzled by the headlights of an oncoming vehicle?
o: Switch the high-beam headlights (if activated) to low beam.
Give a horn signal consisting of one long and three short signals.
Give a horn signal consisting of one short and three long signals.
qs.x: When dazzled, first switch on the hazard lights, then slow down and stop without changing lanes.

qs.q: Horn signals may be used only:
o: In populated areas, to warn other drivers of the intention to pass.
When necessary to prevent a traffic accident.
qs.x: The horn may be used only when needed to prevent an accident.

qs.q: At night, on unlit sections of road, a moving motor vehicle must have the following activated:
qs.x: On unlit roads at night either high or low beam is allowed, high beam when there is no oncoming traffic.

qs.q: Rear fog lights may be used:
o: At night when proceeding as part of a convoy.
Only under conditions of insufficient visibility.
At night when unloading a vehicle.
In all of the listed cases.
qs.x: Rear fog lights may be used only in poor visibility such as fog or heavy rain.

qs.q: At what distance from an oncoming vehicle must high-beam headlights be switched to low beam?
qs.x: High beams must be switched to low at least 150 m from an oncoming vehicle.

qs.q: A searchlight may be used:
o: Only outside populated areas when there are no oncoming or preceding vehicles.
Only under conditions of insufficient visibility.
At night on all sections of road.
qs.x: A searchlight may be used only outside populated areas with no oncoming or preceding vehicles.

qs.q: In populated areas, at what distance before the beginning of a hazardous section is this warning sign installed?
qs.x: In populated areas the Children warning sign is placed 50 to 100 m before the hazard.

qs.q: Is it permitted to transport agricultural, road-construction, construction, and other machines and mechanisms across a railroad crossing?
o: Permitted if the crossing is not equipped with a barrier gate.
Permitted if they are in a non-transport position.
Permitted if they are in a transport position.
qs.x: Farm, road and construction machines may cross a railroad crossing only in transport position.

qs.q: Where is it permitted to cross railroad tracks?
o: At locations where visibility in both directions is at least 1,000 m.
At locations most convenient at the driver’s discretion.
At least 1,000 m from railroad stations.
qs.x: Railroad tracks may be crossed only at designated crossings.

qs.q: While performing an official assignment, is it permitted to open or bypass a barrier gate without authorization?
o: Permitted at the driver’s discretion if no train is approaching nearby.
Permitted if the railroad crossing attendant is absent.
qs.x: Opening or bypassing a barrier on your own is prohibited even on official duty.

qs.q: Is it permitted to transport agricultural, road-construction, construction, and other machines and mechanisms across a railroad crossing?
o: Permitted if they are in a transport position.
qs.x: Machines may cross a railroad crossing only in transport position; otherwise it is prohibited.

qs.q: What must the driver follow when approaching a railroad crossing?
o: The position of the barrier gate and the traffic signals.
The requirements of traffic signs and pavement markings.
The instructions of the railroad crossing attendant.
qs.x: Approaching a crossing the driver must follow all of them: barrier, signals, signs, markings and the attendant.

qs.q: Are pedestrians permitted to proceed on a road marked with the “Freeway” sign?
o: Permitted outside populated areas, against the direction of vehicle traffic.
Permitted outside populated areas, in the same direction as vehicle traffic.
qs.x: Pedestrians are completely prohibited on a road marked as a freeway.

qs.q: Vehicles whose speed, because of their technical characteristics or condition, does not exceed 40 km/h are:
o: Permitted on freeways only in the rightmost lane.
Permitted on freeways if there is no “Minimum Speed Limit” sign.
qs.x: Vehicles that cannot exceed 40 km/h are prohibited from freeways.

qs.q: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
o: In the event of a traffic accident.
In the event of a forced stop where stopping is prohibited.
qs.x: Hazard lights are used both after an accident and for a forced stop where stopping is prohibited.

qs.q: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
o: In the event of a traffic accident.
During towing, on the towed motor vehicle.
In the event of a forced stop where stopping is prohibited.
In all of the listed cases.
qs.x: Hazard lights are required in all listed cases: accident, towed vehicle and forced stop in a prohibited place.

qs.q: At what distance from the vehicle must the emergency warning triangle be placed?
o: At least 15 m in populated areas and at least 30 m outside populated areas.
At least 10 m in populated areas and at least 20 m outside populated areas.
At least 5 m in populated areas and at least 10 m outside populated areas.
qs.x: The warning triangle goes at least 15 m behind the vehicle in towns and at least 30 m outside them.

qs.q: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
o: If the driver is dazzled by headlights.
During towing, on the towed motor vehicle.
qs.x: Hazard lights are used both when dazzled and on a towed motor vehicle.

qs.q: The hazard warning lights on a vehicle must be activated:
o: In the event of a traffic accident.
During towing, on the towed motor vehicle.
qs.x: Hazard lights are used both after an accident and on a towed motor vehicle.

qs.q: In developed areas where the entrance and exit are marked by the “Residential Zone” and “End of Residential Zone” traffic signs, the following is not prohibited:
qs.x: In a residential zone pedestrians may walk on the roadway, while through traffic and driving instruction are prohibited.

qs.q: An intersection is considered controlled if the order of traffic is determined by:
qs.x: An intersection is controlled if priority is set by traffic lights or by a traffic controller.

qs.q: On an unpaved dirt road, does the presence of a paved section immediately before an intersection make that road equal in priority to the intersecting road?
qs.x: A short paved stretch before the junction does not make the dirt road equal to the crossing road; it stays minor.

qs.q: Which image shows the permitted directions of traffic?
qs.x: The right image shows only left, straight and right arrows, while the left and middle ones include the prohibited U-turn.

qs.q: If the meanings of the traffic signals conflict with the requirements of the priority signs, drivers must follow:
qs.x: Traffic signals override priority signs when the two conflict.

qs.q: Is the driver permitted to continue when the yellow traffic signal turns on or the traffic controller raises an arm?
o: Permitted if the driver cannot stop without sudden braking.
qs.x: On yellow or a raised controller's arm you may continue only if you cannot stop without sudden braking.

qs.q: A traffic controller gives a whistle signal:
o: Only when requiring a vehicle to stop.
To attract the attention of road users.
qs.x: A controller's whistle is meant to draw road users' attention.

qs.q: In this situation, is the road train permitted to proceed across the bridge?
qs.x: The sign limits mass to 5 t, and the road train with 5 t on the truck and 4 t on the trailer is heavier, so it may not cross.

qs.q: May a warning signal be given by hand in order to proceed along the indicated path?
o: Yes, if the turn signal is malfunctioning.
Yes, if the turn signal is malfunctioning during daylight hours.
qs.x: A hand signal is allowed when the turn signal is faulty, like the driver in the picture with the arm out.

qs.q: Must the driver activate the turn signal before starting to move in a residential zone?
o: Yes, if other vehicles are present.
qs.x: Signaling before moving off in a residential zone is mandatory, as before any maneuver.

qs.q: To obtain right-of-way over other road users, the driver of a patrol vehicle must activate:
o: The blue and red flashing beacons.
The blue flashing beacon and the special audible signal.
qs.x: A patrol car gets priority only with the blue beacon and special siren on together.

qs.q: Passing is prohibited:
o: At railroad crossings and within 100 m before them.
At railroad crossings and within 150 m before them.
At railroad crossings and within 250 m before them.
qs.x: Passing is prohibited at railroad crossings and within 100 m before them.

qs.q: What does the hand signal given by the passenger-car driver indicate?
o: The driver is making a right turn.
The driver is continuing straight ahead.
qs.x: The driver's raised hand signals braking.

qs.q: The hazard warning lights must be activated:
o: In the event of a traffic accident.
When proceeding as part of an organized convoy.
qs.x: Hazard lights are for a traffic accident, not for entering a tunnel or driving in a convoy.

qs.q: What does the hand signal given by the motorcycle operator indicate?
o: The motorcycle will proceed to the left or make a U-turn.
The motorcycle will proceed straight ahead or to the right.
qs.x: The motorcyclist's arm held straight out to the left signals a left turn or U-turn.

qs.q: What does the hand signal given by the passenger-car driver indicate?
o: The driver is making a right turn.
The driver is continuing straight ahead.
The driver is braking in order to yield to the motorcycle.
qs.x: The driver's left arm out with the forearm bent up signals a right turn.

qs.q: What does the hand signal given by the passenger-car driver indicate?
o: The driver intends to make a left turn or a U-turn.
The driver is braking in order to yield to the truck.
qs.x: An arm held straight out to the left signals intent to turn left or make a U-turn.

qs.x: The picture shows a right turn at a mandatory right-turn sign, and the turn signal must be on before the maneuver.

qs.q: Is the truck driver permitted to pass the bus that is proceeding at a speed of 60 km/h?

qs.q: Is it permitted to enter the railroad crossing in this situation?

qs.q: Is it permitted to enter the railroad crossing in this situation?
o: Permitted if no train is approaching.

qs.x: The red signal is lit and the barrier is lowering, so entering is prohibited even if no train is seen.

o: If no train is approaching, go around the barrier gate and continue.

qs.q: In this situation, is it permitted to cross the railroad crossing?

qs.x: The truck ahead is stopped with brake lights beyond the tracks, so entering is prohibited because you could get stuck on the crossing.

qs.q: In this situation, is it permitted to cross the railroad crossing?
o: Permitted if no train is approaching.
Permitted because the railroad crossing attendant is prohibiting the oncoming vehicle from crossing.
qs.x: The attendant holding a red flag forbids crossing, and the signal applies to everyone, not only the oncoming car.

qs.q: In this situation, where may passing be started?
o: After proceeding 100 m beyond the railroad crossing.
qs.x: Passing may begin only after the crossing, since it is banned on and before it.

qs.q: In this situation, is passing permitted?
o: Permitted because there is no oncoming vehicle.
Permitted if the animal-drawn cart is moving at a speed below 30 km/h.
qs.x: Passing is prohibited in this situation; neither the cart's slow speed nor the lack of oncoming traffic permits it.

qs.q: What maneuver is the passenger-car driver performing?

qs.q: Is passing the motorcycle permitted?

qs.q: On a road with one lane in each direction, when is passing in the oncoming traffic lane permitted?
o: Only when the oncoming traffic lane is clear for a sufficient distance.
Only when no vehicle is passing us.
qs.x: Passing in the oncoming lane requires both a sufficiently clear oncoming lane and that nobody is passing you.

qs.q: Is passing permitted in the indicated situation?

qs.q: If oncoming traffic is difficult in this situation, who must yield?

qs.q: Passing at a pedestrian crossing is:

Only after proceeding ahead of the vehicle in front.
qs.x: The left signal is turned off right after moving into the left lane, because that maneuver is finished.

o: An intention to continue straight ahead.
An intention to make a right turn.
An intention to make a left turn or U-turn.

qs.q: When maneuvering in parking areas or at gas stations, you:

qs.q: Which turn signals must you use when making a U-turn along the indicated path?
qs.x: On this path you first signal right (moving to the edge) and then left for the U-turn itself.

qs.q: If you intend to stop immediately after the intersection, when should you activate the right turn signal so as not to mislead other road users?
qs.x: Signaling right only after entering the intersection avoids suggesting that you will turn at the intersection itself.

qs.q: When changing back into the lane proceeding in the same direction after completing a passing maneuver, does the driver have the right-of-way over a driver already proceeding in that lane?
qs.x: A driver returning to the lane after passing has no priority and must yield to traffic in that lane.

qs.q: Must we yield to a driver exiting an adjacent area with flashing beacons and a special audible signal activated?
qs.x: A vehicle with special light and sound signals has priority, so you must yield to it.

qs.q: When proceeding straight through the intersection, must we yield to the driver of the truck with flashing yellow beacons activated?
qs.x: A flashing yellow beacon gives no priority, it only warns, so you need not yield to that truck.

qs.q: In this situation, to whom must you yield?
o: The driver of the automobile with special light and audible signals activated.
qs.x: The vehicle with special signals has priority over everyone, and a left turn also requires yielding to the oncoming motorcycle.

qs.q: We must yield to:
o: The driver of the truck with a flashing yellow beacon.
qs.x: When turning left you yield to the oncoming bus; the truck with a yellow beacon has no priority.

qs.q: In this situation:
o: You will proceed through the intersection first.
You must yield to the driver approaching from the left.
qs.x: A police car with special signals approaches from the left, so you must yield to it.

qs.q: We must yield to:
o: The driver of the police automobile.
qs.x: A police car with special signals has priority, so you yield to it even on the priority road.

qs.q: When making a left turn:
o: You will proceed through the intersection first.
You will yield only to the driver of the police automobile.
You will yield to all drivers.
qs.x: A left-turning driver yields to oncoming traffic and also to the police car with special signals, so to everyone.

qs.q: When providing first aid to a person with a head injury, you should:
o: Lay the person down with the legs raised.
Lay the person down with the head and torso raised, in a semi-reclined position.
Lay the person flat in a horizontal position.
qs.x: With a head injury, the person is placed in a semi-reclined position with head and torso raised.

qs.q: At a traffic crash, which of the following injured persons should receive assistance first?
o: A man with a fractured arm.
qs.x: An unconscious person is in immediate life-threatening danger (airway risk), so he is helped first.

qs.q: When providing first aid for a nosebleed, you should:
o: Tilt the person’s head forward and pinch the upper part of the nose.
Place a cotton swab in the person’s nose.
Allow the bleeding to continue until it stops on its own.
qs.x: For a nosebleed, tilt the head forward and pinch the nose so blood does not run down the throat.

qs.q: While driving, the driver suddenly begins complaining of severe pressure-like chest pain and difficulty breathing. What should be done?
o: Advise the driver to go to the nearest hospital.
Give the driver a glass of water and two valerian tablets.
Stop the vehicle immediately and activate the hazard warning lights.
Advise the driver to walk a little and breathe fresh air.
qs.x: Severe chest pressure and breathlessness may signal a heart emergency, so stop the vehicle immediately and turn on the hazard lights.

qs.q: What assistance should be provided to a person having a seizure?
o: Hold the person and try to restrain the convulsions.
Try to open the mouth, hold the tongue, and place an object between the teeth.
Try to open the airway by tilting the person’s head back.
Do not interfere; allow the seizure to end.
qs.x: During a seizure do not restrain the person or put anything in the mouth; let it run its course.

qs.q: What should be done when providing first aid for a burn?
o: Open the fluid-filled blisters and then apply a tight bandage.
Cool the burn with water, then cover it with sterile dressing material or clean cloth.
qs.x: Cool the burn with water, then cover it with sterile or clean material; never pop blisters or apply oil.

qs.q: As a result of a crash, a pedestrian has fallen and injured an arm. There is a large wound on the forearm (about 5 cm long) from which dark-colored blood is flowing steadily. What should be done to stop the bleeding?
o: Raise the injured person’s arm and apply a pressure bandage.
Apply an alcoholic iodine solution to the wound.
qs.x: Steady dark blood is venous bleeding: apply a pressure bandage and raise the arm.

qs.q: When providing first aid during the first hours after a closed soft-tissue injury to a limb, you should:
o: Apply a warm compress to the injury.
Apply a cold compress to the injured area and elevate it.
Apply a cold compress to the injured area and keep it below heart level.
Apply an alcohol compress to the injury.
qs.x: In the first hours after a closed injury, apply cold and elevate the limb to reduce swelling.

qs.q: A driver had been crouching for a long time while changing a vehicle’s wheel. After suddenly standing up, the driver grabs the head, loses consciousness, and falls. What should be done?
o: Pour cold water on the driver’s face.
qs.x: For fainting, raise the legs to improve blood flow to the brain.

qs.q: What should be done if the scene cannot be made safe?
o: Provide assistance to everyone, but be careful.
Provide assistance to the injured person who is closest to you.
Do not approach; immediately call for emergency assistance and prevent bystanders from approaching the scene.
Do not approach; ask someone else to provide assistance.
qs.x: If the scene cannot be made safe, do not approach, call for help at once and keep bystanders away.

qs.q: You see a person lying on the ground and notice a bone protruding from the lower leg with bleeding. If the scene is safe, what should be done first?
qs.x: Once the scene is safe, first check consciousness and breathing, as they are the most vital.

qs.q: When an injured person has an open fracture of a limb, first aid requires you to:
o: Cover the wound with a sterile dressing and immobilize the injured limb.
Stop the bleeding by direct pressure.
Apply cold compresses to the wound.
qs.x: For an open fracture, cover the wound with a sterile dressing and immobilize the limb.

qs.q: In case of a chest injury, you should:
o: Lay the injured person in a horizontal position.
Seat the injured person, supporting the injured side.
Seat the injured person, supporting the uninjured side.
qs.x: With a chest injury, seat the person leaning on the injured side to ease breathing.

qs.q: If organs protrude through an open abdominal wound, you should:
o: Wash them and carefully try to place the protruding organs back inside.
Cover the protruding organs with a clean moist cloth and plastic film.
Cut off the protruding organs and bandage the wound.
Do not touch them; transport the injured person to a hospital in that condition.
qs.x: Do not touch or push back protruding organs; cover them with a clean moist cloth and plastic film.

qs.q: An unconscious injured person who is breathing should be:
o: Have the mouth opened and the tongue pulled out.
Turned onto the side with the head tilted back.
qs.x: An unconscious but breathing person is turned onto the side with the head tilted back to keep the airway open.

qs.q: In case of severe bleeding, you should:
o: Only cover the wound with a bandage.
Apply a pressure bandage to the injured area and apply pressure at the arterial pressure point.
qs.x: For severe bleeding, apply a pressure bandage and press the artery at its pressure point.

qs.q: In case of a motor-vehicle crash, the first action should be to:
o: Place the injured person in a comfortable position.
Assess the scene and ensure safety.
Check the injured person for severe bleeding.
Remove the injured person from the vehicle.
qs.x: At a crash, first assess the scene and make it safe.

qs.q: If there is a foreign object in the injured person’s wound, first aid requires you to:
o: Remove the foreign object from the wound.
Allow the injured area to bleed.
Treat the area around the wound with alcohol.
qs.x: Do not remove a foreign object from a wound; keep it immobilized to avoid worsening bleeding.

qs.q: At rest, an adult’s pulse rate is:
qs.x: A resting adult's pulse is 60–80 beats per minute.

qs.q: At rest, an adult’s respiratory rate is:
qs.x: A resting adult breathes 12–18 times per minute.

qs.q: After a crash, an injured person should be removed from the vehicle if:
o: The injured person has serious injuries.
The scene is dangerous, for example, there is a risk of explosion.
An electrical wire has fallen onto the vehicle.
qs.x: An injured person is removed from the vehicle only if the scene is dangerous, e.g., explosion risk.

qs.q: If internal abdominal bleeding is suspected, first aid requires you to:
o: Lay the injured person down and apply a cold compress to the injured area.
Apply a hot-water bottle to the abdomen.
Apply a pressure bandage to the abdomen.
Give the injured person a large amount of fluid.
qs.x: For suspected internal abdominal bleeding, lay the person down and apply cold to the abdomen.

qs.q: You hear a vehicle engine running in your neighbor’s garage. When you open the door, you see your neighbor lying on the floor. What should you do first?
o: Open the doors wide and turn off the engine; if possible, remove the injured person from the scene.
Carefully examine the injured person’s body for injuries.
Turn the injured person onto the side into the recovery position.
Help the injured person into a semi-sitting position.
qs.x: Exhaust gas in the garage is deadly, so first open the doors, turn off the engine and, if possible, remove the person.

qs.q: After finding an unconscious injured person, the first action should be to:
o: Turn the person onto the side into the recovery position.
Maintain the person’s normal body temperature.
Open the airway and check for breathing.
qs.x: For an unconscious person, first open the airway and check breathing.

qs.q: To check circulation in an injured limb, press and release the nail below the bandage. Circulation in the limb is impaired if:
o: The nail is difficult to blanch when pressed.
The nail is slow to return to a pink color.
qs.x: If the nail is slow to turn pink again after pressing, circulation is impaired.

qs.q: Your friend with diabetes feels unwell and cannot remember when insulin was last taken. What should you do first?
o: Give the person sugar or a sweet drink.
qs.x: A diabetic's malaise may be low blood sugar, so first give sugar or a sweet drink.

qs.q: Bleeding is most dangerous if:
o: The blood spurts from the wound.
The blood flows steadily from the wound.
qs.x: Spurting blood is arterial bleeding, the most dangerous because of rapid blood loss.

qs.q: A vehicle has struck a utility pole, and an electrical wire has fallen onto an unconscious injured person lying beside the vehicle. When providing assistance, the first action should be to:
o: Remove the injured person from the source of electrical current.
Remove the wire from the injured person using an insulating object.
Look for electrical entry and exit points (burns) on the body.
qs.x: First remove the hazard: move the wire off the person with an insulating object so the rescuer is not harmed.

qs.q: When providing first aid, to protect yourself from infection, you should:
o: Avoid direct contact with the wound and provide assistance only while wearing sterile gloves.
Do not assist injured persons who are bleeding.
qs.x: To avoid infection, avoid direct contact with the wound and wear sterile gloves.

qs.q: During an asthma attack, an injured person with bronchial asthma should be:
o: Laid down with the legs elevated.
Laid down with the knees bent.
Laid down with the head elevated.
qs.x: During an asthma attack a semi-sitting position makes breathing easier.

qs.q: An injured person with an abdominal injury should be:
o: Laid down with the head elevated.
Laid down with the legs elevated.
Laid down with the knees bent.
qs.x: With an abdominal injury, lay the person down with knees bent to relax the abdominal muscles.

qs.q: In the event of fainting, the injured person should be:
o: Laid down with the legs elevated.
Laid down with the knees bent.
Laid down with the head elevated.
qs.x: For fainting, lay the person down and raise the legs to improve blood supply to the brain.

qs.q: If a low-front vehicle strikes an adult pedestrian who is 1.55 m or taller, injuries are most likely to occur in the:
qs.x: A low-front car hits an adult's legs, and the person then falls onto the hood, so lower limbs and head are injured.

qs.q: If a low-front vehicle strikes a child 3–5 years old, injuries are most likely to occur in the:
qs.x: Because a 3–5 year old is small, a low-front car strikes the pelvis and chest.

qs.q: If an electrical wire has fallen onto a vehicle, you should:
o: Help the occupants get out of the vehicle immediately.
Ask the occupants to remain in the vehicle until the electrical current is disconnected.
qs.x: If a wire lies on a vehicle, occupants should stay inside until the power is cut, since stepping out risks electrocution.

qs.q: When treating minor wounds, you should:
o: Wash the wound with soap and clean water, then bandage it.
Treat the wound with alcohol-containing substances (iodine, vodka, perfume, etc.).
qs.x: Wash a minor wound with soap and clean water and bandage it; alcohol damages tissue.

qs.q: When treating serious wounds, you should:
o: Wash the wound with soap and clean water.
Treat the wound with alcohol-containing substances (iodine, vodka, perfume, etc.).
Stop the bleeding and bandage the wound.
qs.x: For a serious wound the priority is to stop the bleeding and bandage it.

qs.q: In case of a crash, what information should be provided to the emergency dispatcher when requesting an ambulance?
o: State the landmark nearest to the crash location. Report the number of injured persons and indicate their sex and age.
State the street and house number nearest to the crash location. Indicate who was injured in the crash (pedestrian, driver, or passenger) and describe the injuries sustained.

State the crash location (street, house number, and the landmarks nearest to the scene). Report the number of injured persons, their sex, approximate age, state of consciousness, breathing and circulation, and whether there is severe bleeding, fractures, or other injuries. Wait until the dispatcher confirms that the call has been received.
qs.x: Give the dispatcher full details (location, number, sex, age, condition of victims) and wait for confirmation.

qs.q: What is the optimal position for a conscious injured person when a spinal injury is suspected?
o: Lay the injured person on their side.
Lay the injured person on their back on a firm, flat surface; do not move them or change their position unless necessary.
Lay the injured person on their back, place a roll made from clothing under the neck, and raise the legs.
qs.x: With suspected spinal injury, keep the person on the back on a firm flat surface and avoid moving them.

qs.q: How should first aid be provided in case of frostbite and hypothermia?
o: Rub the affected areas of the body with snow or a woolen cloth, then warm them, give the injured person an alcoholic drink, and move them to a warm place.
Warm and immobilize the affected areas of the body, cover the injured person with warm clothing or a blanket, give a warm drink, and move the person to a warm place.
Apply ointment to the affected areas of the body, apply a warming compress and a heating pad, move the injured person to a warm place, and give a warm drink.
qs.x: For frostbite, gently warm and immobilize the affected parts, cover the person and give warm drinks; no rubbing or alcohol.

qs.q: What first aid should be provided for a head injury with a scalp wound?
o: Stop the bleeding by applying direct pressure to the wound and apply a pressure bandage. If the injured person loses consciousness, place them in the recovery position. If possible, apply a cold compress to the injured area of the head.

Immobilize the cervical spine using an improvised splint (collar). Place a sterile cotton pad over the wound and lay the injured person on their back with the legs raised. If possible, apply a cold compress to the head.
A cervical splint must not be applied. Cover the wound with medical adhesive tape and lay the injured person on their side.
qs.x: For a scalp wound, stop bleeding with direct pressure and a pressure bandage, use the recovery position if unconscious, and apply cold.

qs.q: When providing first aid to an unconscious injured person who has circulation and breathing, in what position should the person be placed?
o: On their back, with a roll placed under the head.
On their back, with the legs spread apart.
Place the injured person in the recovery position so that the bent knees touch the ground and the upper hand is positioned under the cheek.
qs.x: A breathing unconscious person is placed in the recovery position to keep the airway open.

qs.q: How long may a tourniquet used to stop bleeding remain in place?
o: In warm weather, no more than half an hour; in cold weather, no more than one hour.
In warm weather, no more than one hour; in cold weather, no more than half an hour.
There is no limit on how long the tourniquet may remain in place.
qs.x: A tourniquet may stay on up to 1 hour in warm weather and 30 minutes in cold weather, to prevent tissue death.

qs.q: How should you determine whether an unconscious injured person is breathing?
o: Hold the injured person by the chin, tilt the head back, and observe chest movement for 10 seconds.

Place one hand on the injured person’s forehead and, with two fingers of the other hand, lift the chin and tilt the head back. For 10 seconds, check for breathing by trying to feel exhaled air on your cheek and observing movement of the chest.
Without tilting the injured person’s head, lean toward the person’s face and, for 10 seconds, check for breathing by trying to feel exhaled air on your cheek and observing movement of the chest.
qs.x: Tilt the head with one hand on the forehead and chin lift, then look, listen and feel for breathing for 10 seconds.

qs.q: What are the main signs of severe arterial bleeding, and what action should be taken first when providing first aid in such a situation?
o: Dark-colored blood slowly flows from the wound. Apply a pressure bandage to the wound and note on it how long it should remain in place.

Bright red blood spurts forcefully from the wound in an intermittent jet or fountain-like stream. Compress the injured artery with your fingers, then apply a tourniquet above the wound, as close to the wound as possible, and note the time it was applied.
Blood slowly flows from the wound. Apply a tourniquet below the injury and note the time it was applied.
qs.x: In arterial bleeding bright red blood spurts: press the artery first, then apply a tourniquet above the wound and note the time.

qs.q: Is it permitted to give medication to an injured person while providing first aid?
o: Permitted in case of extreme necessity.
qs.x: Giving medication to the injured is prohibited during first aid.

qs.q: How should bleeding be stopped in case of injury to veins or small arteries?
o: Apply a pressure bandage directly over the injured area.
Apply a pressure bandage above the wound.
Apply a pressure bandage below the wound.
qs.x: For venous or minor arterial bleeding, apply the pressure bandage directly over the wound.

qs.q: For injuries sustained in a crash, what are the initial first-aid steps?
o: Rinse the wound with water, remove foreign objects from the wound, place sterile cotton on the wound, and secure it with a bandage.
Put on medical gloves, clean the wound with an alcohol solution of iodine, apply medicated ointment, and cover it with adhesive tape.
Put on medical gloves and, without cleaning the wound, cover it with a sterile gauze pad, securing the edges with adhesive tape or a bandage.
qs.x: Put on gloves and cover the wound, without cleaning it, with a sterile gauze pad secured with tape or a bandage.

qs.q: How should first aid be provided for limb fractures when no splints or materials for making a splint are available?
o: Secure the upper limb to the torso with the arm extended along the body. Tie the lower limbs together, placing soft material between them.
With the upper limb bent at the elbow and supported in a sling, secure it to the torso. Tie the lower limbs together, placing soft material between them.
With the upper limb bent at the elbow and supported in a sling, secure it to the torso. Tie the lower limbs together.
qs.x: Without splints, bend the arm at the elbow in a sling and secure it to the torso, and tie the legs together with padding between.

qs.q: In which cases should an injured person be removed from the vehicle?
o: If the vehicle has overturned, caught fire, there is a high risk of explosion, or the injured person has lost consciousness.

If the vehicle has overturned, caught fire, there is a high risk of explosion, or the injured person has hypothermia, has lost consciousness or breathing, or it is impossible to provide first aid directly inside the vehicle.
If the vehicle has overturned, caught fire, there is a high risk of explosion, or the injured person has severe bleeding or a head injury.
qs.x: Remove the person if there is danger (rollover, fire, explosion), hypothermia, loss of consciousness or breathing, or first aid is impossible inside.

qs.q: When providing first aid for a superficial thermal burn (skin redness, swelling, blisters filled with clear fluid at the burn site, and severe pain), what should be done?
o: Pour cold water over the burned area, cover it with a sterile pad, and bandage it tightly.
Open the blisters, remove clothing remnants from the burned area, cover it with a sterile pad without bandaging it, apply a cold compress if possible, and give the injured person water to drink.

Cool the burned area with water for 20 minutes. Without opening the blisters or removing clothing remnants, cover the burned area with a sterile pad without bandaging it, apply a cold compress if possible, and give the injured person water to drink.
qs.x: Cool a superficial burn with water for 20 minutes, do not open blisters, and cover with a sterile pad without bandaging.
